definition_zh: 正确地；恰当地；得体地；彻底地
definition_en: in the correct or suitable way; in a socially acceptable manner; (British, informal) completely or thoroughly
core_image: 工匠把一块木板量准、放平，直到它与墙面严丝合缝
scene: 木工把尺子贴紧墙边，反复对照图纸，确认每一块板都装在该在的位置。 The carpenter checked the shelf twice to make sure it was properly fixed to the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 properly 是「正确地、恰当地」（第 1 个义项：以正确合适的方式）；句意为木匠检查了两次，确认搁板被牢牢固定在墙上。图中可辨识物件：卷尺、图纸、木搁板。

pos.zh: 正确地；恰当地；得体地；彻底地

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到形容词，义为「恰当的；正确的；本身的」
与 proper 同出拉丁 proprius（自己的），义为「得体的举止；合宜」
同出拉丁 proprius（属于自己的东西），义为「财产；房产；属性」
proper 前加否定前缀 im-，义为「不恰当的；不合规矩的」

senses.title: In the correct or suitable way
senses.definition: in the way that is correct, suitable, or expected for a particular purpose
senses.definitionCN: 以正确、合适或符合某一用途所需的方式
senses.example: The machine will not work unless it is properly connected.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器如果没有正确接通，就无法运转。
senses.why: Properly is simply proper plus -ly, so it carries the old Latin sense of something sitting in its own place and fitting there exactly.
senses.whyCN: properly 就是 proper 加 -ly，因此继承了拉丁语「待在自己位置、恰好贴合」的意思：装在该装的地方，才算正确地做。

senses.title: In a socially acceptable manner
senses.definition: in a way that follows good manners or accepted social standards
senses.definitionCN: 遵循良好礼节或公认社会标准的方式
senses.example: He was properly introduced to the guests before dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚宴前，他被正式介绍给各位客人。
senses.why: If a thing belongs in its proper place, a person can also belong in the proper occasion, so the word slides from a fitted joint to fitted behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 东西有它该在的位置，人也有他该在场的场合，于是词义便从「装得对」滑向「举止合宜」。

senses.title: Completely; thoroughly (British, informal)
senses.titleCN: 彻底地；完全地（英式口语）
senses.definition: used in British informal speech to mean completely or very much
senses.definitionCN: 英式口语中表示「完全地、非常」
senses.example: I was properly soaked by the time I got home.
senses.exampleCN: 等我到家时，已经浑身湿透了。
senses.why: When a job is done properly, nothing is left half-finished, so speakers began using the word for utterly or entirely, especially in British speech.
senses.whyCN: 一件事做得 properly，就意味着没有一处半途而废；英式口语便借这层「做得彻底」引申出「完全地」。

senses.title: With good reason; justifiably
senses.definition: in a way that is fair, reasonable, or deserved
senses.definitionCN: 以公平、合理或应得的方式
senses.example: She was properly proud of the garden she had raised from seed.
senses.exampleCN: 那座花园是她从种子一手养大的，她理应为之自豪。
senses.why: Something proper is fitting, and what is fitting can also be deserved, which lets the word mark fair pride or fair blame rather than mere correctness.
senses.whyCN: proper 指「合宜」，而合宜的东西也就是应得的；于是这个词能标示理所应当的自豪或责备，而不只是「正确」。

intro.en: Properly is the adverb of proper, a word that reached English from Latin proprius by way of French, with -ly added to mark the manner of doing something.
intro.cn: properly 是 proper 的副词形式；proper 经法语来自拉丁语 proprius，加上 -ly 表示做事的方式。

items.en: Proprius meant one's own, special, or belonging to a particular thing rather than to others.
items.cn: proprius 意为「自己的、专属的」，指某物属于特定对象，而不属于别的对象。

items.en: The noun proprietas named the quality of belonging to someone, and it later split into English propriety and property.
items.cn: 名词 proprietas 表示「归属某人的性质」，后来在英语中分化出 propriety 与 property。

items.en: Old French kept the adjective as propre, meaning own, suitable, or clean, and passed it into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语保留形容词 propre，意为「自己的、合适的、干净的」，诺曼时期之后传入英语。

items.en: Middle English proper meant belonging to a person or thing and also fitting or correct, the sense that survives in proper behaviour.
items.cn: 中古英语 proper 既指「属于某人或某物的」，也指「合适的、正确的」，后一义保留在 proper behaviour 中。

items.en: English added the adverb ending -ly to proper, giving properly, which marks the manner of doing something in the right way.
items.cn: 英语在 proper 后加副词后缀 -ly 得到 properly，用来标示「以正确方式做某事」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin stem proprius; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs for doing something the right way.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁词干 proprius 上的词；近义组收表示「以正确方式做事」的副词。

entries.definition: Correct, suitable, or belonging to a particular thing.
entries.definitionCN: 正确的、合适的，或属于某一特定事物的。

entries.definition: Not correct, or not acceptable in polite company.
entries.definitionCN: 不正确的，或在礼貌场合不被接受的。

entries.definition: Behaviour that follows accepted social standards.
entries.definitionCN: 符合公认社会标准的举止；得体。

entries.definition: Something owned by a person, or a quality of a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 某人拥有的财物，或某物的属性。

entries.definition: In a way that is accurate and free from error.
entries.definitionCN: 准确、没有错误地。

entries.definition: In a way that suits the situation or purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 以适合情境或目的的方式。

entries.definition: In a way that is right for the occasion.
entries.definitionCN: 适合该场合地。

entries.definition: For a good reason, or in a fair way.
entries.definitionCN: 有充分理由地，或公平地。

normalIntro.en: The word is built from the Latin adjective proprius, its French descendant propre, and the ordinary English adverb ending -ly.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由拉丁形容词 proprius、它的法语后裔 propre，以及最常见的英语副词后缀 -ly 组成。

normal.en: Properly is proper plus -ly, and -ly is the ordinary English ending for the manner of an action.
normal.cn: properly 就是 proper 加 -ly，而 -ly 是英语里最常见的「做事方式」后缀。

normal.en: Something proper sits in its own place, so doing a job properly means putting every part where it belongs.
normal.cn: proper 的东西待在属于自己的位置，所以把事情做得 properly，就是把每个部分放到该放的地方。

normal.en: Improper is proper with the negative prefix im-, so improper behaviour is the exact opposite of proper behaviour.
normal.cn: improper 是 proper 前加否定前缀 im-，所以不得体的行为正是得体行为的反面。

normal.en: Property and propriety share one stem: one is what belongs to you, the other is what belongs to good manners.
normal.cn: property 与 propriety 同根：前者是归属于你的东西，后者是归属于良好礼节的东西。

normal.en: The phrase properly speaking marks the strict or exact use of a word, which is the correct sense of the adverb.
normal.cn: 短语 properly speaking 标示一个词的严格、准确用法，这正是这个副词「正确」的一面。

abstract.en: A joint that clicks into place is the whole idea of properly: no force left over, no gap left open.
abstract.cn: 一个卡进槽里的榫头就是 properly 的全部意象：用不上多余的力，也留不下一道缝。

abstract.en: The word moves easily from a fitted shelf to a fitting remark, because both are judged by one question: does it belong here?
abstract.cn: 这个词可以从装好的搁板滑到一句合适的话，因为两者面对同一个判断：它属于这里吗？

abstract.en: When British speakers say properly soaked, they mean soaked through, which shows how correctness can slide into completeness.
abstract.cn: 英国人说 properly soaked 时意思是湿透，可见「正确」可以滑向「彻底」。

examples.en: The shelter must be properly anchored before the storm arrives.
examples.cn: 暴风雨来临前，这个庇护所必须被妥善固定。

examples.en: She was properly dressed for the interview.
examples.cn: 她为面试穿得很得体。

examples.en: He was properly ashamed of what he had said.
examples.cn: 他对自己说过的话理当感到羞愧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普若婆利」——把每样东西摆回它该在的地方，事情才算做得对。

root: 拉丁语 proprius（自己的、专属的）→ 古法语 propre → 英语 proper；proper 加副词后缀 -ly 得 properly，义为「以正确、合宜的方式」。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is fitting into the right place; from there the word spreads to social manners, to complete thoroughness, and to what is deserved.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「装进正确的位置」；义项由此扩展到社交礼节、彻底的完成，以及理所应得。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a board measured, levelled and fixed so that it sits exactly where it should.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块木板被量准、找平、固定，正好落在它该在的位置。

branches.en: a shelf fixed with a level and a tape measure
branches.cn: 用水平尺和卷尺装好的搁板

branches.en: a guest greeted in the right order at dinner
branches.cn: 晚宴上按次序向客人致意

branches.en: rain soaking a coat through to the lining
branches.cn: 雨水把外套从里到外浸透

branches.en: a gardener standing back from a bed she raised
branches.cn: 园丁退后一步，看着自己养大的花圃

branches.en: one word judging a fitted joint and a fair pride
branches.cn: 同一个词既评判装好的接缝，也评判应得的自豪

intro.en: The word is held together by the Latin adjective proprius, its French descendant propre, and the English adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁形容词 proprius、它的法语后裔 propre，以及英语副词后缀 -ly 共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 月；月份；一个月的时间；漫长的岁月（复数）
definition_en: one of the twelve divisions of the year, also a period of about thirty days and, in the plural, a long stretch of time
core_image: 日历上撕下的一页，边缘还留着月亮的弧度
scene: 月底的夜里，桌上的账单摊开，日期一格一格逼近。 The rent falls due at the start of every month.
sceneCN: 这里是「月份、月」（第 1 个义项：日历上的一年十二分之一）；句意为每到月初房租就到期。图中可辨识物件：账单、日历、台灯。

pos.zh: 月；月份；一个月的时间；漫长的岁月

derivatives.zh: 由 month 加 -ly 构成，义为「每月的；每月一次」
由 month 与 long 复合而成，义为「持续一个月的」
由前缀 bi-（两个）加 monthly 构成，义为「两月一次的」

senses.title: One of the twelve divisions of the year
senses.definition: one of the twelve named divisions of the calendar year
senses.definitionCN: 日历年里十二个有名称的划分之一
senses.example: February is the shortest month of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 二月是一年里最短的月份。
senses.why: A month began as the moon's own cycle, so the word for the unit still carries the shape of a turning moon.
senses.whyCN: 月份最初就是月亮自己的一轮周期，所以这个表单位的词里仍留着月亮转动的形状。

senses.title: A period of about thirty days
senses.definition: a span of roughly thirty days used as a unit of time
senses.definitionCN: 用作计时单位的大约三十天的一段时间
senses.example: The repairs took a month to finish.
senses.exampleCN: 修理工作花了一个月才完成。
senses.why: Once the unit is fixed, it can measure any span of about thirty days, whether or not the calendar page matches.
senses.whyCN: 单位一旦固定，它就能用来量任何约三十天的时间段，不必与日历那一页严格对齐。

senses.title: A long stretch of time, in the plural
senses.definition: a long time, used in the plural to suggest a slow wait
senses.definitionCN: 很长的一段时间，用复数来表示漫长的等待
senses.example: She has not written to us for months.
senses.exampleCN: 她好几个月没有给我们写信了。
senses.why: Counting months is slow, so a plural pile of them naturally stands for a long wait.
senses.whyCN: 按月计数本来就慢，于是复数的月份自然就表示一段漫长的等待。

senses.title: The lunar cycle
senses.definition: the period from one new moon to the next, about twenty-nine and a half days
senses.definitionCN: 从一个新月到下一个新月的周期，约二十九天半
senses.example: A lunar month lasts about twenty-nine and a half days.
senses.exampleCN: 一个太阴月约持续二十九天半。
senses.why: The moon-based origin keeps a technical sense alive in astronomy, where a lunar month runs from one new moon to the next.
senses.whyCN: 以月亮为起点的来源让一个术语义在天文学里保留下来：太阴月从一个新月走到下一个新月。

intro.en: The English month is a Germanic word built on the moon, and its oldest sense is a moon-driven cycle rather than a page on a wall.
intro.cn: 英语的 month 是建立在月亮之上的日耳曼词，它最早的意思是被月亮推动的一轮周期，而不是墙上的一页纸。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to measure is generally thought to lie behind the words for moon and month in both the Germanic and the Latin branches.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个表示「测量」的印欧语重构词根同时藏在日耳曼语和拉丁语中表示月亮与月份的词后面。

items.en: Old English mōnaþ joined mōna, the moon, with the noun suffix -þ, so the month was literally the moon's turning.
items.cn: 古英语 mōnaþ 把 mōna（月亮）与名词后缀 -þ 结合，所以月份字面上就是月亮的一轮转动。

items.en: Related forms such as Old Frisian mōnath and German Monat show the same moon-based naming across the Germanic languages.
items.cn: 古弗里斯兰语的 mōnath、德语的 Monat 等相关形式显示，日耳曼各语言都用月亮来命名月份。

items.en: Middle English moneth kept the moon inside the word while the spelling slowly moved toward the modern month.
items.cn: 中古英语的 moneth 仍把月亮留在词里，拼写则慢慢向现代形式 month 靠拢。

items.en: Modern English month covers the calendar unit, the lunar cycle and, in the plural, a long stretch of time.
items.cn: 现代英语的 month 兼指日历单位、月相周期，复数还表示很长一段时间。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the same moon stem, while the near-meaning group collects the other units used to count time.
note.cn: 形近组收同一月亮词干上的形式，近义组收用来计时的其他单位。

entries.definition: Happening once every month or issued each month.
entries.definitionCN: 由 month 加 -ly 构成，义为「每月的；每月一次」。

entries.definition: The body whose cycle gave the month its name.
entries.definitionCN: 其周期为月份提供名称的天体，月亮。

entries.definition: The day named after the moon, from the same Old English stem.
entries.definitionCN: 以月亮命名的日子，来自同一个古英语词干。

entries.definition: A period of seven days, the unit just below a month.
entries.definitionCN: 七天的一段时间，是比月更小的计时单位。

entries.definition: A period of twelve months.
entries.definitionCN: 十二个月的一段时间。

entries.definition: A period of two weeks, common in British usage.
entries.definitionCN: 两周的一段时间，英式用法中常见。

entries.definition: A period of twenty-four hours.
entries.definitionCN: 二十四小时的一段时间。

normalIntro.en: The word is a moon-word from start to finish, and its family keeps returning to cycling light and counted time.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从头到尾都是月亮词，它的同族词也一直回到光的循环与被数出来的时间。

normal.en: Old English mōnaþ is moon plus a noun ending, so the month was named after the moon that paced it.
normal.cn: 古英语 mōnaþ 是月亮加一个名词词尾，月份是用给它定节奏的月亮命名的。

normal.en: German Monat and Dutch maand keep the same m-n shape, which is why the English word looks so plain.
normal.cn: 德语 Monat 与荷兰语 maand 保留同样的 m-n 骨架，所以英语这个词显得格外朴素。

normal.en: monthly adds -ly to month: something that happens once in each month.
normal.cn: monthly 在 month 后加 -ly，表示在每个月发生一次的事物。

normal.en: The plural months often means a long time, as in letters unanswered for months.
normal.cn: 复数的 months 常表示很久，例如好几个月没有回信。

normal.en: Latin mensis is a distant cousin rather than a borrowing, which is why English did not take a Latin shape.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mensis 是远亲而不是借词，所以英语没有采用拉丁语的词形。

abstract.en: A calendar is a row of moons, each one handing its name to a page.
abstract.cn: 日历就是一排月亮，每一个把自己的名字交给一页纸。

abstract.en: Turn a page and a moon has already happened.
abstract.cn: 翻过一页，就有一轮月亮已经走完。

abstract.en: The word is older than paper: people counted months by looking up.
abstract.cn: 这个词比纸更老：人们曾靠抬头看天来数月份。

examples.en: February is the shortest month of the year.
examples.cn: 二月是一年里最短的月份。

examples.en: The repairs took a month to finish.
examples.cn: 修理工作花了一个月才完成。

examples.en: She has not written to us for months.
examples.cn: 她好几个月没有给我们写信了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「忙死」——月底事情多到忙死；记住 month 就是月。

root: 古英语 mōnaþ 由 mōna（月亮）加名词后缀 -þ 构成，本义是月亮的一轮；一般认为它与拉丁语 mensis 同出印欧语表示「测量」的词根。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the calendar unit, and the senses then branch into a measured span, a slow plural of waiting, and the lunar cycle underneath it all.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是日历上的月份；义项由此分出被丈量的时间段、表示漫长等待的复数，以及藏在底下的月相周期。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a page torn from a calendar, its edge still curved like a moon.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张从日历上撕下的纸，边缘仍带着月牙的弧度。

branches.en: a calendar page torn off on the first day
branches.cn: 月初撕下的一页日历

branches.en: a repair job stretching across thirty days
branches.cn: 一项横跨三十天的修理活

branches.en: letters left unanswered for a season
branches.cn: 一整个季节无人回的信

branches.en: a chart tracing new moon to new moon
branches.cn: 从新月画到新月的图

branches.en: rent falling due as a month turns
branches.cn: 月份交替时到期的房租

intro.en: The word is held together by a moon noun, an old noun ending, and the two suffixes that turn it into a monthly adjective.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示月亮的名词、一个古老的名词词尾，以及把它变成「每月的」形容词的两个后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin mensis and menstruus belong to the same distant Indo-European family, though English borrowed nothing directly from them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mensis 与 menstruus 属于同一遥远的印欧语族，但英语并没有直接借用它们。

items.meaningCN: 构成形容词与副词的后缀

items.meaning: the body that paces the month

items.meaningCN: 由 moon 与 day 复合

definition_zh: 一半；半个；（足球）半场；（副词）一半地
definition_en: one of two equal parts of something
core_image: 一块饼从正中切开，两半完全一样大
scene: 妈妈把刚出炉的披萨从正中切开，兄弟俩一人一半。 Half of the pizza went to each brother.
sceneCN: 这里 half 是「一半」（第 1 个义项：二等分之一）；句意是半个披萨分给了每位兄弟。

derivatives.zh: 由 half + way 构成，义为「在中途；半路」
由 half + hearted 构成，义为「半心半意的；敷衍的」

senses.title: One of two equal parts
senses.definition: either of two equal parts into which something is divided
senses.definitionCN: 某物被平分成的两部分之一
senses.example: She ate half of the cake.
senses.exampleCN: 她吃了蛋糕的一半。
senses.why: The picture is one clean cut, so the first sense is the equal share itself.
senses.whyCN: 画面是干脆的一刀，第一个义项就是平分后的那份。

senses.title: A part roughly dividing something
senses.definition: a part that divides something into two roughly equal pieces
senses.definitionCN: 把某物大致分成两半的部分
senses.example: Half the students agreed and half did not.
senses.exampleCN: 一半学生同意，一半不同意。
senses.why: Real cuts are rarely perfect, so half tolerates unequal shares.
senses.whyCN: 现实中难得切得完美，half 便容纳了不均的份。

senses.title: A sports period
senses.definition: one of two equal periods of a game
senses.definitionCN: 比赛分成两个相等时段之一
senses.example: The team scored twice in the first half.
senses.exampleCN: 该队上半场进了两球。
senses.why: A match is cut in two by time, exactly like the knife cuts the cake.
senses.whyCN: 比赛被时间一分为二，正如刀切蛋糕。

senses.title: A quantity less than whole
senses.definition: partly but not completely done or felt
senses.definitionCN: 部分地、未完全地完成或感受
senses.example: He gave a half smile and looked away.

items.en: Middle English half widened into fractions, sports periods, and adverbs.

items.en: Modern English fixed the plural halves and compounds like halfway.

definition_zh: 真实的；真正的；实际的；十足的
definition_en: actually existing and not imagined; genuine and not false; practical rather than theoretical; complete or utter, used for emphasis
core_image: 照片旁边的实物带着可以触摸的质地
scene: 桌上摆着一张照片和一枚同样的果子，果子拿在手里沉甸甸的。 The painting looks real enough to touch.
sceneCN: 这里 real 是「真实的」（第 1 个义项：实际存在、非想象）；句意为这幅画逼真得仿佛可以触摸。画面里可留意：照片与实物、手中沉甸甸的果子。

pos.zh: 真实的；真正的；实际的；十足的

derivatives.zh: real 加 -ly，指真正地、确实
real 加 -ity，指现实、真实性
real 加 -istic，指现实的、逼真的
real 加 -ize，指意识到、实现

senses.title: Actually existing
senses.definition: actually existing in the world, not imagined or invented
senses.definitionCN: 确实存在于世上，而非想象或虚构
senses.example: The painting looks real enough to touch.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画逼真得仿佛可以触摸。
senses.why: Real comes from Latin res, a thing, so the adjective first marks what is a thing and not a mere image.
senses.whyCN: real 来自拉丁语 res（事物），因此这个形容词首先标记「是事物而非单纯影像」的东西。

senses.title: Genuine
senses.definition: genuine and not false, imitation or counterfeit
senses.definitionCN: 真的，而非虚假、仿制或伪造
senses.example: Is that a real diamond or a copy?
senses.exampleCN: 那是真钻石还是仿制品？
senses.why: A thing that truly exists can be told apart from a copy, so real came to mean genuine rather than fake.
senses.whyCN: 真正存在之物能与仿制品区分，于是 real 引申为「真的」而非假的。

senses.title: Practical
senses.definition: concerned with actual conditions rather than theory or imagination
senses.definitionCN: 关涉实际状况，而非理论或想象
senses.example: We need a real solution, not another promise.
senses.exampleCN: 我们需要实际的解决办法，而不是又一个承诺。
senses.why: What exists as a thing also exists in practice, so real extended from reality to practical effectiveness.
senses.whyCN: 作为事物存在的东西也在实践中存在，于是 real 从「现实」扩展到「实际有效」。

senses.title: Complete, for emphasis
senses.definition: used informally to emphasize a quality, often a bad one
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用于强调某种性质，常为负面
senses.example: That was a real mess.
senses.exampleCN: 那真是一团糟。
senses.why: In casual speech the word for what truly exists became a general intensifier, marking something as fully and unmistakably so.
senses.whyCN: 在口语中，表示「真正存在」的词变成一般强调词，标记某物完全且不容置疑地如此。

intro.en: Real comes from Latin realis, belonging to res, a thing; English borrowed it to mark what exists as a thing rather than as an image or a word.
intro.cn: real 来自拉丁语 realis，意为属于 res（事物）的；英语借它来标记「作为事物存在」而非影像或词语的东西。

items.en: Res meant a thing, a matter or a fact, the plainest word for what exists.
items.cn: res 意为事物、事情或事实，是表示「存在之物」最朴素的词。

items.en: Realis meant belonging to a thing, and it described what has actual existence.
items.cn: realis 意为属于事物的，形容具有实际存在的东西。

items.en: English took realis as real, setting what is real against what is imagined or copied.
items.cn: 英语把 realis 借作 real，把真实之物与想象或仿制之物相对。

items.en: Because a real thing is not a copy, the word grew to mean genuine, and then practical rather than theoretical.
items.cn: 由于真实之物不是复制品，这个词引申为「真正的」，再引申为「实际的」而非理论的。

items.en: Modern English uses real for existence, genuineness, practical effect, and informal emphasis.
items.cn: 现代英语用 real 指存在、真实、实际效果，以及口语中的强调。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on real; the near-meaning group gathers words for what truly exists or is genuine.
note.cn: 形近组收由 real 构成的形式；近义组收表示真实存在或名副其实的词。

senses.title: Not asleep
senses.definition: not asleep, with the mind alert
senses.definitionCN: 没有睡着，心神清醒
senses.example: I was awake most of the night.
senses.exampleCN: 我大半夜都醒着。
senses.why: The prefix marks a state and wake means to rise from sleep, so not sleeping is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 前缀标记状态，wake 意为从睡眠中起身，所以没有睡着就是第一义。

senses.title: Knowing what is happening
senses.definition: aware of something that is happening or may happen
senses.definitionCN: 察觉到正在发生或可能发生的事
senses.example: The town is awake to the danger of fires.
senses.exampleCN: 全镇都意识到了火灾的危险。
senses.why: A mind fully out of sleep is open to what goes on, which gives the sense of being aware.
senses.whyCN: 完全脱离睡眠的心对周围保持开放，于是有「意识到」的义项。

intro.en: The recorded history of awake is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.

items.cn: 前缀 a- 意为处于或在上。

items.en: English joined the prefix and the verb into awake.
items.cn: 英语把前缀与动词合成 awake。

entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指醒着的时候。

entries.definition: It stresses quick attention to danger.
entries.definitionCN: 强调对危险的敏锐注意。

entries.definition: It stresses being unable to sleep.
entries.definitionCN: 强调无法入睡。

entries.definition: It stresses being aware rather than awake.
entries.definitionCN: 强调有意识，而非醒着。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: a- means in and wake means to rise from sleep: awake is the state of having risen.
normal.cn: a- 表示处于，wake 表示从睡眠中起身：awake 就是已经起身的状态。

normal.en: The same family also gives wake and awaken.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 wake 与 awaken。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase stay awake.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「保持清醒」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of awake in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 awake 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: not asleep, or knowing that something is happening.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「醒着的」时用它。

abstract.en: Picture a person lying in bed at night with open eyes.
abstract.cn: 想象夜里一个人睁着眼睛躺在床上。

abstract.en: The same picture can be literal in one sentence and figurative in another.
abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

examples.en: I was awake most of the night.
examples.cn: 我大半夜都醒着。

examples.en: The town is awake to the danger of fires.
examples.cn: 全镇都意识到了火灾的危险。

examples.en: She stayed awake until the train came.
examples.cn: 她一直醒着，直到火车到达。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿韦克」——夜里睁眼躺在床上：醒着的

root: awake 由古英语前缀 a-「处于」与 wacan「醒来」合成，十四世纪起形容脱离睡眠的人，今天也指意识到某种危险。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of awake grows from one core image: a person lying in bed at night with open eyes.
sensesIntro.cn: awake 的各个义项都从同一个核心意象生长出来：夜里一个人睁着眼睛躺在床上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person lying in bed at night with open eyes
core.cn: 核心意象：夜里一个人睁着眼睛躺在床上

branches.en: Sense 01 covers the most literal use: Not asleep.
branches.cn: 义项 01 覆盖最字面的用法：醒着的。

branches.en: Sense 02 covers a wider everyday use: Knowing what is happening.
branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更宽泛的日常用法：意识到、警觉的。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 02 covers the two main uses: Not asleep / Knowing what is happening.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 02 覆盖两个主要用法：醒着的、意识到、警觉的。

branches.en: Sense 02 covers a further use: Knowing what is happening.
branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更靠后的一种用法：意识到、警觉的。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 02 covers the outer edge of the meaning: Not asleep / Knowing what is happening.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 02 覆盖意义的边缘：醒着的、意识到、警觉的。

intro.en: awake can be split into the parts below, which also connect it to common English patterns.
intro.cn: awake 可以按下面的成分拆开，这些成分也把它与常见的英语构词方式连起来。

latinIntro.en: No recorded Latin cognate is securely attached to this word, so the list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠记录的拉丁同族词可以系在这个词上，因此该列表留空。

items.example: It gives the sense of leaving sleep.
items.exampleCN: 它给出「脱离睡眠」的意思。

items.example: It marks a plural noun in English.
It marks the past tense or a completed state.
items.exampleCN: 它标记过去时或已完成的状态。

items.example: It forms the present participle of a verb.
items.exampleCN: 它构成动词的现在分词。

items.example: It turns an adjective into an adverb.
It names the doer of an action.
items.exampleCN: 它指做某动作的人或物。

items.example: It turns an adjective into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成表状态的名词。

definition_zh: 家具；（总称）设备；内在装备
definition_en: movable objects such as chairs, tables, and beds that make a room usable
core_image: 搬进新居时一屋子等待摆位的桌椅床柜
scene: 搬家卡车停在楼下，木箱贴着「易碎」标签。 The new flat looked empty until the furniture arrived in the afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 furniture 是「家具」（第 1 个义项：房间内可移动的用具）；句意为下午家具运到之前，新公寓看起来空荡荡的。

collocations.zh: 头脑中的知识储备（比喻）

forms.label: 无词形变化（不可数名词）

derivatives.zh: furniture 的同源动词，义为「布置家具；供应」
furnish 加名词后缀 -er 构成，义为「供应者；家具商」

senses.title: Movable room equipment
senses.definition: movable articles such as tables, chairs, and beds that equip a room
senses.definitionCN: 桌椅床柜等可移动的房间装备
senses.example: They sold their old furniture before moving abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 移居国外前他们卖掉了旧家具。
senses.why: The word names the whole set of movable equipment, so the room-image sits at the center.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名整套可移动装备，因此「房间」的画面居于中心。

senses.title: Equipment of an organization
senses.definition: the useful parts or fittings of an organization, vehicle, or system
senses.definitionCN: 机构、车辆或系统中的实用部件或配置
senses.example: Good research needs the furniture of grants, labs, and journals.
senses.exampleCN: 好的研究离不开经费、实验室与期刊这些配套设施。
senses.why: A room needs furniture to work; an organization likewise needs its fittings, so the image extends.
senses.whyCN: 房间需要家具才能使用，机构同样需要配套，画面由此延伸。

senses.title: Mental equipment
senses.definition: the stock of ideas or knowledge a mind contains
senses.definitionCN: 头脑中储存的思想或知识
senses.example: Logic is part of the furniture of a trained mind.
senses.exampleCN: 逻辑是受过训练的头脑的一部分储备。
senses.why: The mind is pictured as a room furnished with ideas, a borrowed interior.
senses.whyCN: 头脑被想象为用思想陈设的房间，是一种借用的内部空间画面。

senses.title: Wood-worked movable goods
senses.definition: furniture viewed especially as worked wood or joinery
senses.definitionCN: 特指以木作工艺制成的器物
senses.example: This village is known for hand-carved furniture.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子以手工雕刻木器闻名。
senses.why: Historically most furniture was wood, so a craft sense remains attached.
senses.whyCN: 历史上家具多为木制，因此保留着一个手工艺义项。

senses.title: Fixed fittings by extension
senses.definition: built-in fittings that cannot be moved, used loosely alongside furniture
senses.definitionCN: 与家具并称的不可移动的内装设施
senses.example: The rent includes curtains, lights, and fitted furniture.
senses.exampleCN: 房租包含窗帘、灯具与固定家具。
senses.why: Lists of room contents blur the movable and fixed, so the edge of the sense widens in trade speech.
senses.whyCN: 房屋清单中可动与固定常混列，商业用语放宽了义项边界。

intro.en: Furniture came from French, built on a verb meaning to supply or fit out.
intro.cn: furniture 来自法语，建立在意为「供应、装备」的动词之上。

items.en: Old French furnir meant to supply, complete, or fit out.
items.cn: 古法语 furnir 意为供应、备齐、装备。

items.en: French furnir is of Germanic origin, generally traced to a Frankish root.
items.cn: 法语 furnir 源自日耳曼语，一般认为可追溯到法兰克语词根。

items.en: Middle English borrowed furniture in the sixteenth century for the act of furnishing.
items.cn: 中古英语在十六世纪借入 furniture，指「装备行为」。

items.en: The sense narrowed from equipment in general to movable household goods.
items.cn: 词义从泛指装备收窄为可移动的家居用品。

items.en: The related verb furnish kept the wider supplying sense.
items.cn: 同源动词 furnish 保留了更宽的「供应」义。

note.en: Furniture is uncountable, and learners often meet its near neighbours in house language.
note.cn: furniture 不可数，学习者常在家居语言中遇到它的近邻。

entries.definition: to supply a room with furniture
entries.definitionCN: 布置家具；furniture 的同源动词

entries.definition: an enclosed chamber for heating
entries.definitionCN: 炉子；拼写开头相近但词源无关

entries.definition: the time to come
entries.definitionCN: 未来；拼写局部相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a powered household device
entries.definitionCN: 家用电器；带电源的设备，与家具分工

entries.definition: a fixed part of a building
entries.definitionCN: 固定装置；与可动家具相对

entries.definition: tools or items needed for a purpose
entries.definitionCN: 装备；泛指一切器材

normalIntro.en: Five grounded hooks for furniture.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实词形的 furniture 记忆钩子。

normal.en: Furniture is uncountable: say a piece of furniture, never furnitures.
normal.cn: furniture 不可数：说 a piece of furniture，不能加 s。

normal.en: The verb furnish is inside the word: to furnish is to fill with furniture.
normal.cn: 词里藏着动词 furnish：furnish 就是用家具布置。

normal.en: Furni- begins like furnace, but furniture lives in rooms, furnaces in basements.
normal.cn: 词头像 furnace，但 furniture 在房间，furnace 在地下室。

normal.en: The -ture ending marks the French borrow, like picture and nature.
normal.cn: -ture 词尾标记法语借词，同 picture、nature。

normal.en: Furniture of the mind is a set metaphor worth remembering.
normal.cn: the furniture of one's mind 是值得记住的固定比喻。

abstract.en: Picture a bare room filling with table, chairs, and bed one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象空房间里桌椅床一件件落位。

abstract.en: Hear the soft -ture ending, like a drawer sliding closed.
abstract.cn: -ture 的发音像抽屉轻轻关上。

abstract.en: See the mind as a room where ideas are the chairs and lamps.
abstract.cn: 把头脑想成房间，思想是其中的椅子与灯。

examples.en: We bought a piece of furniture for the hallway.
examples.cn: 我们为门厅买了一件家具。

examples.en: Moving house means boxing up all the furniture.
examples.cn: 搬家意味着把所有家具装箱。

examples.en: The study is part of the furniture of his mind.
examples.cn: 这门学问是他头脑储备的一部分。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗尼彻」——家具还没彻齐，先请弗尼彻先生来布置。

root: 古法语 furnir（供应、装备，源于日耳曼语）→ 法语 furniture（装备物）→ 英语 furniture；核心语义是「供房间使用的一切装备」。

sensesIntro.en: Household movables are the center; organizational fittings, mental stock, and craft senses extend outward.
sensesIntro.cn: 家居可动用品是中心；机构配置、头脑储备与木作工艺义项向外延伸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a room made usable by its movable gear
core.cn: 核心意象：靠可动装备变得可用的房间

branches.en: contents of a room, movable or fitted
branches.cn: 房间内容物：可动与固定

branches.en: what an organization runs on
branches.cn: 机构运转的配套

branches.en: ideas stocked in the mind
branches.cn: 头脑中的思想储备

branches.en: joinery and carved wood
branches.cn: 木作与雕件

branches.en: goods made for living space
branches.cn: 为居住空间而制的器物

intro.en: The furn- root carries the supplying idea through the family.
intro.cn: 词根 furn- 把「供应」之意贯穿整个词族。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic in origin, so Latin relatives are absent.
latinIntro.cn: 词根源于日耳曼语，因此没有拉丁同源词。

items.exampleCN: 他们低成本布置了办公室。

items.example: The furnisher delivered all desks on time.
items.exampleCN: 家具商按时送来了所有桌子。

items.meaning: the result or means of an action
items.example: Furniture, picture, and nature share the ending.
The furniture in this cafe is handmade.
items.exampleCN: 这家咖啡馆的家具是手工的。

items.example: The -ure ending often marks borrowed nouns.
The shop sells curtains and furnishings.
items.exampleCN: 这家店出售窗帘和陈设用品。

items.meaning: the soft fittings of a room
items.exampleCN: 明亮的软装让房间生暖。

items.example: They refurnished the lounge last year.
items.exampleCN: 他们去年重新布置了休息室。
前缀 re- 表示重复。

definition_zh: 混合；搅合；调配；交往；混合物
definition_en: to combine different things into one mass, to prepare something by blending ingredients, to spend time with others, or the blend itself
core_image: 两管不同颜色的颜料挤进同一只白碟，被勺子搅成一团新的颜色
scene: 画室的桌上摆着两管颜料，学生把颜色挤在同一只碟里。 On the studio table the student squeezed two colours into one dish and began to mix them with a spoon.
sceneCN: 这里是「混合」（第 1 个义项：把不同东西搅在一起）；句意为学生把两种颜色挤进同一只碟子，用勺子开始搅。图中可辨识物件：两管颜料、白瓷碟、调色勺。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干 mixt- 加 -ure 构成，义为「混合物」
由 mix 加 -er 构成，义为「搅拌器；调酒师」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「混合的；褒贬不一的」

senses.title: To combine separate things into one mass
senses.definition: to put different substances or things together and stir or blend them so that they form one whole
senses.definitionCN: 把不同的物质或东西放在一起搅动、拌合，使它们成为一个整体
senses.example: Mix the sand and cement before adding water.
senses.exampleCN: 加水和之前，先把沙与水泥搅拌在一起。
senses.why: Latin miscere meant to blend, and the word still begins with two things that were separate and are now folded into each other.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 miscere 意为混合；这个词的起点始终是两样原本分开的东西，此刻互相折了进去。

senses.title: To prepare something by blending ingredients
senses.definition: to make a drink, dough or other preparation by measuring and combining its parts
senses.definitionCN: 按分量把各组成部分合在一起，做出饮料、面团或其他制品
senses.example: She mixed a bowl of batter for the pancakes.
senses.exampleCN: 她调了一碗做薄饼的面糊。
senses.why: Once blending is a deliberate act, it can serve a recipe: the cook measures first and folds second, so the same verb covers both the stirring and the thing being made.
senses.whyCN: 当混合成了一种有意的动作，它就可以为一份食谱服务：先量、后拌；于是同一个动词既管搅动，也管做出来的东西。

senses.title: To spend time and talk with other people
senses.definition: to be with other people socially, especially at a gathering
senses.definitionCN: 在社交场合与他人相处、交谈，尤指在聚会上
senses.example: At the reception he mixed easily with guests he had never met.
senses.exampleCN: 招待会上，他和从未见过的客人也能自在地交谈。
senses.why: People in a room are separate individuals until conversation folds them into a group; the social sense borrows exactly that picture of separate units becoming one gathering.
senses.whyCN: 满屋子的人原本是一个个分开的个体，谈话把他们折进同一个群体；社交义借的正是「分开的单位合成一个场合」这幅画。

senses.title: A blend, or a packet of ready-measured ingredients
senses.definition: a combination of different things, or a commercial packet in which the dry parts of a recipe are already combined
senses.definitionCN: 不同东西的组合，或商店里把一份食谱的干料预先配好的包装
senses.example: The stall sells a soup mix that needs only hot water.
senses.exampleCN: 那个摊位卖一种汤料包，只需加热水。
senses.why: When the verb's result is treated as a thing, it becomes a noun: whatever came out of the bowl, or the packet that saves the cook the measuring.
senses.whyCN: 当动词的结果被当成一件东西，它就变成名词：可以是碗里拌出来的成品，也可以是替厨师省去称量的那袋配料。

intro.en: Mix goes back through Latin miscere and its participle mixtus; English first used mixt as an adjective and later formed the short verb mix from it.
intro.cn: mix 经由拉丁语 miscere 及其分词 mixtus 而来；英语先用 mixt 作形容词，后来又从它反推出简短动词 mix。

items.en: Miscere meant to mix or blend, and it supplied the participle that carried the idea into several European languages.
items.cn: miscere 意为混合、拌合，它提供的分词把这一概念送进了欧洲的好几种语言。

items.en: The past participle mixtus described something already blended, and Old French kept a form of it as mixte.
items.cn: 过去分词 mixtus 描述已经混好的东西，古法语保留了它的一个形式 mixte。

items.en: English used mixt as an adjective and participle for a blended substance, following the French form rather than the Latin spelling.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语用 mixt 作形容词与分词，指已经混合的物质，拼写跟着法语而不是拉丁语。

items.en: A short verb mix was formed from mixt by dropping the final t, and the first records are generally dated to the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 简短的动词 mix 一般认为是在十六世纪由 mixt 去掉词尾的 t 反推而成，最早的记录也定在这个世纪。

items.en: The verb spread into cooking, chemistry and music, while the noun mix named both the blend and the packet of measured dry ingredients.
items.cn: 这个动词扩展到烹饪、化学与音乐；名词 mix 既指混好的东西，也指配好分量的干料包。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin-derived relatives and the English derivatives; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of joining substances or people.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁来源的同族词与英语派生词；近义组收表示把物质或人合到一起的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for a blended result, built on the Latin stem mixt- with -ure.
entries.definitionCN: 表示混合结果的名词，由拉丁词干 mixt- 加 -ure 构成。

entries.definition: A machine or a person that mixes, formed by adding -er to the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 搅拌的机器或人，由动词加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: The past participle used as an adjective, meaning blended or of more than one kind.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词转作形容词，指混合的，或由不止一种构成的。

entries.definition: To mix things so smoothly that the parts are no longer easy to tell apart.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西混得十分均匀，以致不易分辨各组成部分。

entries.definition: To bring two or more things together, often while each keeps its own identity.
entries.definitionCN: 把两样或更多东西合在一起，往往各自仍保留特性。

entries.definition: To mix with people at a gathering, or for things to flow together.
entries.definitionCN: 在聚会上与人交往，或指事物交融在一起。

normalIntro.en: The word comes from a Latin verb of blending, and its family keeps returning to the moment separate parts lose their edges.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语中表示混合的动词，同族词反复回到「分开的部分失去边界」的那一刻。

normal.en: Miscere is the Latin verb for blending, and mixture keeps its stem mixt- in plain view.
normal.cn: miscere 是拉丁语中表示混合的动词，mixture 把它的词干 mixt- 明明白白保留着。

normal.en: Mix was clipped from mixt, an older participle, so the verb is younger than the adjective it came from.
normal.cn: mix 是从较早的分词 mixt 截短而来，所以这个动词比它所出的形容词更年轻。

normal.en: A cake mix is the recipe before the cook: the dry parts are already combined in the packet.
normal.cn: cake mix 是厨师动手之前的食谱：干料已经在袋子里配好了。

normal.en: Mix with people uses the social sense of the same picture: separate persons folded into one gathering.
normal.cn: mix with people 用的是同一幅画的社会义：分开的人被折进同一个场合。

normal.en: Mixed feelings are feelings of more than one kind stirred together, which is the adjective's everyday life.
normal.cn: mixed feelings 是两种以上情绪搅在一起，正是这个形容词的日常用法。

abstract.en: Nothing in the word says the parts must disappear, only that they now share one space.
abstract.cn: 这个词没有说各部分必须消失，只说他共享了同一个空间。

abstract.en: Cooking, chemistry and conversation all use the same verb because all three are about boundaries giving way.
abstract.cn: 烹饪、化学与交谈都用同一个动词，因为三者都在说边界让开。

abstract.en: A mixture is a small argument for the value of difference: the result is neither part alone.
abstract.cn: 混合物是差异之价值的一个小小论据：结果既不是原来的任何一方。

examples.en: Mix the flour and water until the dough is smooth.
examples.cn: 把面粉和水混合，直到面团变得光滑。

examples.en: He mixed a little lime juice into the drink.
examples.cn: 他在饮料里调进了一点青柠汁。

examples.en: She finds it hard to mix with strangers at parties.
examples.cn: 她觉得在聚会上很难与陌生人打交道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米克斯」——把米和克都倒进一只碗里搅匀，就是混合。

senses.title: The two-wheeled pedal vehicle
senses.definition: a vehicle with two wheels in line, moved by pedals and steered by handlebars
senses.definitionCN: 一种两轮前后排列、靠脚踏驱动、用把手转向的车
senses.example: He rides his bicycle to school every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他每天早上骑自行车上学。
senses.why: The name joins bi-, two, with cycle, wheel, so it literally says two wheels, which is the plainest description of the machine.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字把表示「二」的 bi- 与表示「轮」的 cycle 合在一起，字面就是「两个轮子」，正是对这种车最直白的描述。

senses.title: To ride a bicycle
senses.definition: to travel or move by bicycle
senses.definitionCN: 骑自行车出行或移动
senses.example: She bicycled across the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 她骑自行车过了桥。
senses.why: The verb is the noun turned into action: using the two-wheeled machine to get somewhere.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词转成动作：用这种两轮车去到某个地方。

senses.title: Used as a modifier
senses.definition: used before another noun to mean intended for or belonging to bicycles
senses.definitionCN: 用在另一个名词前，表示供自行车使用或属于自行车的
senses.example: The bicycle lane is painted green.
senses.exampleCN: 自行车道被刷成了绿色。
senses.why: English lets a noun stand before another noun like an adjective, so bicycle before lane simply marks what the lane is for.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许名词像形容词一样放在另一个名词前，所以 lane 前的 bicycle 只是标记这条道是给谁用的。

intro.en: Bicycle is a nineteenth-century coinage built from a Latin prefix and a Greek word for wheel.
intro.cn: bicycle 是十九世纪造出的词，由拉丁语前缀与希腊语「轮」合成。

items.en: French coined bicyclette in the nineteenth century from bi-, two, and cycle, wheel.
items.cn: 法语在十九世纪用 bi-「二」与 cycle「轮」造出 bicyclette。

items.en: The first part is the Latin prefix bi-, meaning two, related to bis, twice.
items.cn: 第一部分是拉丁语前缀 bi-，意为「二」，与 bis「两次」相关。

items.en: The second part goes back to Greek kyklos, a circle or a wheel.
items.cn: 第二部分可追溯到希腊语 kyklos，意为「圆圈、轮子」。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the age of the pedalled machine and shortened it to bicycle.
items.cn: 英语在脚踏车流行的年代借入这个词，并缩短为 bicycle。

items.en: Everyday speech soon clipped it to bike, which became the common short form.
items.cn: 日常口语很快把它截短为 bike，此后成为常用的简短形式。

items.en: Today bicycle is the formal word, and it also works as a verb and as a modifier.
items.cn: 今天 bicycle 是正式用词，也可作动词和定语。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the short form and the trike family; the near-meaning group collects other small wheeled vehicles.
note.cn: 形近组收简短形式与三轮车一族；近义组收其他小型轮式交通工具。

entries.definition: The clipped everyday word for a bicycle or motorcycle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「自行车、摩托车」，是 bicycle 的日常截短形式。

entries.definition: A wheel word used in bicycle, and also a verb meaning to ride.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「轮、循环」，是 bicycle 的后半成分，也可作动词表示「骑车」。

entries.definition: A three-wheeled pedal vehicle, built with tri-.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「三轮车」，由 tri-「三」构成。

entries.definition: A person who rides a bicycle.

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「两轮车」，是泛指的说法。

entries.definition: A small motor vehicle with pedals and a low engine.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「轻便摩托车」，带脚踏和小排量发动机。

entries.definition: A small two-wheeled vehicle that the rider stands or sits on.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「踏板车、小轮摩托」，骑者站在或坐在上面。

entries.definition: A heavy two-wheeled vehicle driven by an engine.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「摩托车」，由发动机驱动的重型两轮车。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded parts, the real family, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的构件、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Bi- means two and cycle means wheel, so bicycle is simply two wheels.
normal.cn: bi- 表示「二」，cycle 表示「轮」，所以 bicycle 就是「两个轮子」。

normal.en: Tricycle adds tri-, three, and unicycle adds uni-, one; the family is easy to see.
normal.cn: tricycle 换成 tri-「三」，unicycle 换成 uni-「一」，这个词族一眼就能看清。

normal.en: Everyday speech shortens it to bike, which is the word you hear most.
normal.cn: 日常口语把它缩短成 bike，这是最常听到的说法。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with ride, lane, pump and shop.
normal.cn: 它常与 ride、lane、pump、shop 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-i-c-y-c-l-e: two c's and one y, with the y between them.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-i-c-y-c-l-e：两个 c，中间夹一个 y。

abstract.en: See two wheels in a line with a chain running between them: that is bicycle.
abstract.cn: 想象两个轮子前后排列，中间有一条链条，那就是 bicycle。

abstract.en: Turn the same picture into a verb and the wheels start moving under a rider.
abstract.cn: 把同一幅画变成动词，两个轮子就在骑者脚下转起来。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the turning wheels bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让转动的车轮把意思带回来。

examples.en: He rides his bicycle to school every morning.
examples.cn: 他每天早上骑自行车上学。

examples.cn: 她骑自行车过了桥。

examples.en: The bicycle lane is painted green.
examples.cn: 自行车道被刷成了绿色。

root: bicycle 是十九世纪的造词，来自法语 bicyclette，由拉丁语前缀 bi-「二」与希腊语 kyklos「轮」合成，字面就是「两个轮子」。英语借入后缩短为 bicycle，口语又进一步截成 bike。名词可作定语，也可直接转动词表示「骑自行车」。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses of bicycle are one machine seen three ways: the thing itself, the act of riding it, and its use as a modifier.
sensesIntro.cn: bicycle 的三个义项是同一台车的三种看法：车本身、骑它的动作，以及它作定语时的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two wheels in a line joined by a chain
core.cn: 核心意象：两个前后排列、由链条相连的轮子

branches.en: THE MACHINE: two wheels and pedals make the object itself.
branches.cn: 机器线：两个轮子加脚踏，构成这件器物本身。

branches.en: THE MOTION: the same machine turning into an action becomes the verb.
branches.cn: 动作线：同一台车转成动作，就成了动词。

branches.en: THE PURPOSE: placed before lane or shop, the noun marks what something is for.
branches.cn: 用途线：放在 lane 或 shop 前，这个名词标记某物的用途。

branches.en: THE PAIR: the object and its action share one word in English.
branches.cn: 成对线：器物与动作在英语里共用同一个词。

branches.en: THE RIDER: the moving picture always needs a person on the seat.
branches.cn: 骑者线：会动的画面里总要有一个坐在座上的人。

intro.cn: bicycle 是由拉丁语前缀与「轮」词构成的现代复合词，其构件在许多其他词里也能产。

definition_zh: 他们；她们；它们；泛指的人（如 everyone...they）
definition_en: the people, animals, or things already mentioned, or people in general when the exact person is unknown
core_image: 一群人站在远处，你指向他们：不是你，不是我，是他们
scene: 孩子们在操场上踢球，喊声传到教室。 They are still playing football after the last bell.
sceneCN: 这里 they 是「他们」（第 1 个义项：指前文提到的一群人）；句意：放学铃响后他们还在踢球。

pos.zh: 泛指某人；那个人们（单数用法）

derivatives.zh: 他们（宾格；与 they 同属一个代词词形变化表）
他们的（所有格；与 there、they're 同音，注意区分）

他们自己（反身代词，由 them 加 selves 构成）

senses.title: The people already mentioned
senses.titleCN: 他们；她们：指前文说过的那些人
senses.definition: the group of people, animals, or things that has just been spoken or written about, as subject of the verb
senses.definitionCN: 刚被提到的人群、动物或事物，在句中作主语
senses.example: The students finished the exam, and they went out to celebrate.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们考完试，就出去庆祝了。
senses.why: A sentence already names its people once; they steps in so the names need not be repeated.
senses.whyCN: 一句话只需把人名点一次；they 替补上场，省得反复报名字。

senses.title: Things or animals
senses.definition: used for animals or things in the plural, or for a single animal whose sex is unknown
senses.definitionCN: 用于复数的动物或事物，或性别不明的单个动物
senses.example: The books arrived late, but they were all undamaged.
senses.exampleCN: 书到得晚了，但全都完好无损。
senses.why: The old plural pointing word covers every third-person plural that is not us or you, without asking about species.
senses.whyCN: 这个古老的复数指示词包揽一切既非我们也非你们的第三人称复数，不问物种。

senses.title: People in general
senses.definition: people in general, or an unspecified person, especially after words like everyone, somebody, or nobody
senses.definitionCN: 泛指一般人，或身份不明的某个人，尤其跟在 everyone、somebody、nobody 之后
senses.example: If anybody calls, tell them I am in a meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 如果有人打电话，告诉那人我在开会。
senses.why: When the exact person is unknown or unimportant, English borrows the plural form because it carries no marking of gender.
senses.whyCN: 当具体是谁不重要时，英语借用复数形式，因为它不带任何性别标记。

senses.title: A single person of unspecified gender
senses.definition: one person whose gender is not stated or is not relevant, as in a doctor...they
senses.definitionCN: 性别未说明或无关紧要的某一个人，如 a doctor...they
senses.example: A good teacher listens before they speak.
senses.exampleCN: 好老师先倾听再开口。
senses.why: Written English since the Middle Ages has allowed they for one unknown person; modern usage has revived and extended this old right.
senses.whyCN: 自中古英语起，书面语就允许用 they 指身份不明者；现代用法复兴并扩展了这一古老权利。

intro.en: They is a Norse loan. Old English had hie for they, but the Scandinavian settlers' word their, from the same ancient stem as that, pushed it out almost everywhere.
intro.cn: they 是古诺斯语借词。古英语本来用 hie 表示「他们」，但斯堪的纳维亚移民带来的、与 that 同源的 their 一词几乎把它挤出了所有方言。

items.en: Old Norse Their meant they, built on the demonstrative stem tha- that also produced the and that.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 Their 意为「他们」，建立在指示词干 tha- 之上；the、that 也出自同一词干。

items.en: Old English used hie, with forms like heora for their and him for them; the system was starting to blur by sound change.
items.cn: 古英语用 hie 表「他们」，所有格是 heora，与格是 him；语音演变已让这套代词开始混淆。

items.en: In the Danelaw, Norse settlers spoke a close cousin of English; their pronouns were easier to tell apart and were adopted in the north first.
items.cn: 在丹麦法区，诺斯移民说的语言与英语是近亲；他们的代词更易分辨，于是在北部最先被采用。

items.en: Middle English spread they, their and them from north to south, replacing most of the old hie forms by the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，they、their、them 由北向南推广，到十五世纪基本取代了旧的 hie 系列形式。

items.en: Standard English settled the paradigm they, them, their, theirs, and later added the singular use now written about as singular they.
items.cn: 标准英语固定了 they、them、their、theirs 的范式，后来又发展出如今被称为 singular they 的单数用法。

note.en: The first group lines up the same-sounding pronoun pair; the second collects the other personal pronouns of English.
note.cn: 第一组是同音易混的代词；第二组是英语其他人称代词。

normalIntro.en: Real hooks: the Norse origin, the full paradigm they them their theirs, and the sound-alike trio.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：古诺斯语来源、they them their theirs 完整范式、以及同音三兄弟。

normal.en: They came from the Vikings: Old Norse their replaced the old English hie.

normal.en: The paradigm: they do, them see, their book, theirs is red, themselves.
normal.cn: 范式：they 作主语，them 作宾语，their 表所属，theirs 独立用，themselves 反身。

normal.en: They, their, there, they're: four spellings, three sounds, endless exam questions.
normal.cn: they、their、there、they're：四种拼法，三个读音，考题无穷。

normal.en: They say is how English quotes the crowd without naming it.

normal.en: Everybody...they: the singular they has been legal in English for six centuries.
normal.cn: everybody 后接 they：单数 they 在英语里合法了六个世纪。

abstract.en: They is the crowd seen from a distance, one shape for every mixture.

abstract.en: A pronoun is a loan of attention: you lend your name once, and they carries it.
abstract.cn: 代词是注意力的借贷：名字只需出借一次，they 替你背着它走。

abstract.en: When we do not know who, English shrugs and says they.
abstract.cn: 当不知道是谁时，英语耸耸肩说 they。

sensesIntro.en: They first replaces a named group, then covers plural animals and things, and finally serves for people in general and for one person whose gender does not matter.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a group standing at a distance, pointed at with one short word.

branches.en: The core job: subject pronoun for a known group.

branches.en: The plural reaches animals and things without asking.

branches.en: Generic they quotes the crowd: they say.

branches.en: Both extensions come from the same neutrality: no gender, no species, no fuss.

senses.title: Very great in amount

definition_zh: 死；死亡；消失；熄灭
definition_en: to stop living; to stop existing or working
core_image: 灯火摇曳几下后归于平静
scene: 爷爷在院子里讲他年轻时的故事，说到老屋的旧灯。 The old lantern finally died after many years of service.
sceneCN: 这里 die 是「熄灭、失效」（第 2 个义项：停止运作）；句意是服役多年的旧灯笼终于熄灭了。

senses.title: To stop living
senses.definition: to stop being alive
senses.definitionCN: 停止生存
senses.example: The old cat died quietly in its sleep last winter.
senses.exampleCN: 去年冬天，老猫在睡梦中安静地离世。
senses.why: Life leaves a body the way a flame leaves a wick.
senses.whyCN: 生命离开躯体，如同火苗离开灯芯，归于平静。

senses.title: To stop working or existing
senses.definition: to stop working, burning or existing gradually
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐停止运作、燃烧或存在
senses.example: The engine died in the middle of the road.
senses.exampleCN: 发动机在路中间熄火了。
senses.why: Machines and fires lose their life too, so they are said to die.
senses.whyCN: 机器与火焰也有「生命」，失去动力便被说成 die。

senses.title: To want something very much
senses.definition: to want something so much that you feel desperate, informal
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示极度渴望
senses.example: After the long run, I was dying for a glass of water.
senses.exampleCN: 长跑之后，我特别想喝一杯水。
senses.why: Strong want feels like a small death of patience.
senses.whyCN: 强烈的渴望让耐心几乎「死去」，口语便用 die 夸张表达。

intro.en: Die came from Norse words for passing away.
intro.cn: die 来自古诺尔斯语中表示「逝去」的词。

items.en: The Norse word deyja meant to pass away.

items.cn: 古英语原有 steorfan 一词，后来变成 starve（饿死）。

items.en: Die became the plain everyday verb for stopping to live.
items.cn: die 成为表示死亡最平实常用的动词。

items.en: Spelling settled at four letters, kept distinct from dye.
items.cn: 拼写定为四字母，与 dye（染色）区分。

definition_zh: 快乐；喜悦；乐事
definition_en: a strong feeling of happiness, or a person or thing that causes it
core_image: 一个人听见好消息，脸上的光一下子亮起来
scene: 门口传来钥匙转动的声音，孩子跑过去，扑进刚下班的父母怀里。 Her face lit with joy when the letter arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 joy 是「喜悦」（第 1 个义项：强烈的快乐情绪），句意为信到时她脸上立刻亮起喜悦。画面里的物件：门口、信件、灯光。

senses.title: A strong happy feeling
senses.definition: a deep feeling of delight and gladness
senses.definitionCN: 深切的喜悦与高兴
senses.example: The children shouted with joy when the snow began.
senses.exampleCN: 雪一下起来，孩子们就欢呼起来。
senses.why: The first sense is the feeling itself, with no object attached.
senses.whyCN: 第一个义项是情绪本身，不牵扯具体对象。

senses.title: A source of happiness
senses.definition: a person or thing that brings great pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 带来极大快乐的人或事物
senses.example: That old cat is the joy of her life.
senses.exampleCN: 那只老猫是她生活里的欢乐。
senses.why: English often turns a feeling word into the thing that causes it.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把表示感受的词转成引起感受的那个东西。

senses.title: Success in informal speech
senses.definition: a sense of achievement, mostly in the phrase "no joy"
senses.definitionCN: 取得成效的感觉，多见于 no joy 这一说法
senses.example: We tried twice and got no joy, so we called again.
senses.exampleCN: 我们试了两次都没成功，只好又打电话。
senses.why: In informal speech the word also measures whether an attempt worked.
senses.whyCN: 在口语里，这个词还用来衡量一次尝试有没有成。

intro.en: Joy comes from Old French joie, from Latin gaudium, "gladness", from the verb gaudere, "to rejoice".
intro.cn: joy 来自古法语 joie，源自拉丁语 gaudium「喜乐」，后者来自动词 gaudere「欢乐」。

items.en: gaudere meant "to be glad, to rejoice".
items.cn: gaudere 意为「高兴、欢欣」。

items.en: The noun gaudium meant "gladness".
items.cn: 名词 gaudium 意为「喜乐」。

items.en: French softened it to joie.
items.cn: 法语把它软化成 joie。

items.en: English took joie as joy and kept the feeling sense.
items.cn: 英语借作 joy，保留了情感义。

items.en: Idioms like "jump for joy" fixed the word in everyday speech.
items.cn: jump for joy 一类成语把它固定在日常语里。

note.cn: 形近组共用 j- 开头与同一情感家族；近义组收表示快乐的词。

entries.definition: Great pleasure, often sudden.

entries.definition: A quiet state of being pleased.

entries.definition: The general state of being happy.

senses.why: Acting inside a group becomes the sense of taking part willingly.
senses.whyCN: 把行动放在群体里，就成了积极参与。

senses.title: The grammar form
senses.definition: describing a sentence where the doer comes first
senses.definitionCN: 描述执行者位于句首的句子
senses.example: Write the sentence in the active voice.
senses.exampleCN: 把这个句子写成主动语态。
senses.why: Grammar uses active for the voice in which the doer is put first, because the subject is doing the action.
senses.whyCN: 语法把执行者在前的语态叫主动语态，因为主语正在做这个动作。

intro.en: The recorded history of active is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 active 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Agere meant to do, and its participle gave the idea of doing.
items.cn: agere 意为做，它的分词给出「正在做」的意思。

items.en: Activus meant busy or working, built from the verb.
items.cn: activus 意为忙碌的、运作的，由这个动词构成。

items.en: Old French carried the adjective toward English.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词带向英语。

items.en: English used active for busy people and working things.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪用 active 指忙碌的人与运作的事物。

items.en: Today it also names volcano states and grammar forms.
items.cn: 今天它也指火山状态与语法形式。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: The adverb for doing something with energy.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，指积极地做某事。

entries.definition: The noun for things people do.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指人们做的事。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to make something work.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，意为使某物运作。

entries.definition: It stresses full, cheerful movement.
entries.definitionCN: 强调充满活力的活动。

entries.definition: It stresses having much to do.
entries.definitionCN: 强调有许多事要做。

entries.definition: It stresses strong physical energy.
entries.definitionCN: 强调旺盛的体力。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: act means to do and -ive means tending to: active means tending to do things.
normal.cn: act 表示做，-ive 表示倾向于：active 就是倾向于做事的。

normal.en: The same family also gives actively and activity.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 actively 与 activity。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase stay active.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「保持活跃」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of active in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 active 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: doing things, moving a lot, or working in a full way.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「活跃的」时用它。

abstract.en: Picture children running everywhere on a playground.
abstract.cn: 想象操场上到处奔跑的孩子。

abstract.en: The same picture can be literal in one sentence and figurative in another.
abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

examples.en: She is active in class.
examples.cn: 她在课堂上很活跃。

examples.en: He is an active member of the club.
examples.cn: 他是俱乐部的积极成员。

examples.cn: 把这个句子写成主动语态。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of active grows from one core image: children running everywhere on a playground.
sensesIntro.cn: active 的各个义项都从同一个核心意象生长出来：操场上到处奔跑的孩子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: children running everywhere on a playground
core.cn: 核心意象：操场上到处奔跑的孩子

branches.en: Sense 01 covers the most literal use: Busy and energetic.
branches.cn: 义项 01 覆盖最字面的用法：活跃而有精力。

branches.en: Sense 02 covers a wider everyday use: Taking part willingly.
branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更宽泛的日常用法：积极参与的。

branches.en: Sense 03 covers a further use: The grammar form.
branches.cn: 义项 03 覆盖更靠后的一种用法：主动语态的。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 02 covers the two main uses: Busy and energetic / Taking part willingly.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 02 覆盖两个主要用法：活跃而有精力、积极参与的。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 03 covers the two main uses: Busy and energetic / The grammar form.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 03 覆盖两个主要用法：活跃而有精力、主动语态的。

intro.en: active can be split into the parts below, which also connect it to common English patterns.
intro.cn: active 可以按下面的成分拆开，这些成分也把它与常见的英语构词方式连起来。

latinIntro.en: No recorded Latin cognate is securely attached to this word, so the list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠记录的拉丁同族词可以系在这个词上，因此该列表留空。

items.example: It comes from agere, meaning to do.

items.exampleCN: 它构成表倾向的形容词。

items.example: It marks a plural noun in English.
It marks the past tense or a completed state.
items.exampleCN: 它标记过去时或已完成的状态。

items.example: It forms the present participle of a verb.
items.exampleCN: 它构成动词的现在分词。

items.example: It turns an adjective into an adverb.
It names the doer of an action.
items.exampleCN: 它指做某动作的人或物。

items.example: It turns an adjective into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成表状态的名词。

definition_zh: 重复；重说；重做；复述
definition_en: to say or do the same thing more than once
core_image: 同一句话从嘴里第二次、第三次说出来，像回声绕回来
scene: 老师没听清答案，让学生再说一遍，学生于是重复了刚才那句话。 The teacher asked him to repeat the sentence more slowly.
sceneCN: 这里 repeat 是「重说；重复」（第 1 个义项：把说过的话再说一次）；句意：老师让他把这句话再慢慢重复一遍。

derivatives.zh: 重复；反复
重复的；乏味的
反复地
可重复的
反复的

senses.title: To say something again
senses.definition: to say or write something again, either once more or several times
senses.definitionCN: 把说过或写过的话再说一遍或说好几遍
senses.example: Could you repeat the last question?
senses.exampleCN: 你能把最后一个问题再说一遍吗？
senses.why: The core of the Latin verb is to seek again, so going back over the same words is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词的核心意思是「再次寻求」，所以回到同一句话上就是第一个义项。

senses.title: To do something again
senses.definition: to do an action or performance again
senses.definitionCN: 把某个动作或表演再做一次
senses.example: The team repeated the experiment to check the result.
senses.exampleCN: 团队重做了实验来核对结果。
senses.why: Once repeating is about going over something again, it easily moves from words to actions.
senses.whyCN: 既然重复是「再走一遍」，它就很容易从言语扩展到动作。

senses.title: To happen again
senses.definition: to happen again in the same way
senses.definitionCN: 以相同的方式再次发生
senses.example: History often repeats itself in small ways.
senses.exampleCN: 历史常常以细微的方式重演。
senses.why: When an event returns in the same pattern, people describe it as repeating itself.
senses.whyCN: 当一件事以同样的模式再次出现，人们就说它「重演」。

intro.en: Repeat comes from Latin repetere, to seek again, formed from re-, again, and petere, to seek.
intro.cn: repeat 来自拉丁语 repetere（再次寻求），由 re-（再次）与 petere（寻求）构成。

items.en: Petere means to seek, head for, or attack, and it supplies the central stem.
items.cn: petere 意为寻求、前往或攻击，提供核心词干。

items.en: Repetere adds re-, again, and means to go back for something or say it over.
items.cn: repetere 加上 re-（再次），意为回去取某物或把话再说一遍。

items.en: The noun repetitio names the act of going over something again.
items.cn: 名词 repetitio 指把某事再过一遍的动作。

items.en: Old French repeter keeps both the spoken and the renewed-action senses.
items.cn: 古法语 repeter 保留了「重说」和「重做」两种意思。

items.en: Middle English repeat enters through French and is used for words, deeds, and events.
items.cn: 中古英语 repeat 经法语进入，用于言语、行为和事件。

items.en: Modern English adds the noun use for a repeated broadcast or performance.
items.cn: 现代英语又增加名词用法，指重播节目或重演。

note.en: Repeat is the plain verb of doing something again, and its family includes the nouns and adjectives built from the same Latin stem.
note.cn: repeat 是表示「再做一次」的朴素动词，其词族包括由同一拉丁词干构成的名词和形容词。

entries.definition: the act of repeating something
entries.definitionCN: 重复；反复

entries.definition: done or said many times in the same way
entries.definitionCN: 重复的；反复的

entries.definition: many times, again and again
entries.definitionCN: 反复地；一再地

entries.definition: to say something again for emphasis
entries.definitionCN: 重申；反复说

entries.definition: to say something again in a clearer way
entries.definitionCN: 重新表述

entries.definition: to repeat a sound or someone's words
entries.definitionCN: 回响；附和

entries.definition: to make an exact copy of something
entries.definitionCN: 复制；重复

normalIntro.en: Repeat can be heard as re- plus peat, and the second part sounds like beat, so the word feels like hitting the same note again.
normalIntro.cn: repeat 可以听成 re- 加 peat，后半截又像 beat，于是整个词像把同一个音再敲一遍。

normal.en: Re- means again, and the rest of the word is the thing being said: say it again.
normal.cn: re- 表示再次，后面那部分是所说的内容：再说一次。

normal.en: Repeat after me is the classroom phrase that fixes the word in memory.
normal.cn: repeat after me 是课堂用语，最容易把这个词记牢。

normal.en: History repeats itself turns the word from speech to events.
normal.cn: history repeats itself 把这个词从言语转到事件。

normal.en: Compare repetition: the noun adds -ition and keeps the same stem.
normal.cn: 对比 repetition：名词加 -ition，词干不变。

normal.en: Repeat the mistake is a common phrase, so the word can carry a warning.
normal.cn: repeat the mistake 是常见搭配，所以这个词也能带警告意味。

abstract.en: Picture a parrot that says the same phrase at the same time every morning.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鹦鹉每天早晨同一时间说同一句话。

abstract.en: Imagine a song stuck in your head returning to the same line.
abstract.cn: 想象一首歌在脑中循环，总回到同一句。

abstract.en: Think of footprints walking back over their own path in the snow.
abstract.cn: 想象雪地上的脚印沿着原路又走了一遍。

examples.en: Please repeat your name for the record.
examples.cn: 请再说一遍你的名字，以便记录。

examples.en: The class repeated the drill until everyone could do it.
examples.cn: 全班反复练习这个动作，直到每个人都会做。

examples.en: The same argument was repeated at every meeting.
examples.cn: 同样的争论在每次会议上都重复出现。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞皮特」——瑞气重复得特别多；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再次）+ petere（寻求）→ repetere（再次寻求、重说）→ 古法语 repeter → 中古英语 repeat。

sensesIntro.en: One motion of going back over something produces three senses: the same words again, the same action again, and the same event returning.
sensesIntro.cn: 「把某事再走一遍」这一个动作生出三个义项：同样的话再说、同样的动作再做、同样的事件再次出现。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same sound or action returning to the starting point.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个声音或动作回到起点，再走一遍。

branches.en: Saying the same words once more is the basic verbal sense.
branches.cn: 把同样的话再说一次，是最基本的言语义项。

branches.en: The repetition moves from speech to action and performance.
branches.cn: 重复从言语扩展到动作和表演。

branches.en: When events return in the same pattern, the word describes history repeating.
branches.cn: 当事件以同样模式返回，这个词就描述历史重演。

branches.en: Words and actions share the same return motion.
branches.cn: 言语和动作共享同一个「返回」动作。

branches.en: A repeated action and a recurring event both form a cycle.
branches.cn: 反复的动作与循环的事件都构成一个周期。

intro.en: Repeat is a Latin verb built from a prefix and a root, with its noun and adjective family formed by English endings.
intro.cn: repeat 是由前缀和词根构成的拉丁动词，其名词与形容词词族由英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: The prefix re- means again, and petere means to seek or go toward.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 re- 表示再次，petere 表示寻求或前往。

items.example: Re- appears in repeat and return.
items.exampleCN: re- 出现在 repeat 和 return 中。

items.example: Petere is the root of repeat and petition.
items.exampleCN: petere 是 repeat 与 petition 的词根。
repetere 由 re- 与 petere 合成。

items.example: Repetitio is the Latin noun behind repetition.
items.exampleCN: repetitio 是 repetition 背后的拉丁名词。

items.example: Repeat carries the Latin verb into English.
items.exampleCN: repeat 把拉丁动词带入英语。

items.example: Repetition adds -ition to the Latin stem.
Repetitive adds -ive to the same stem.
Repeatedly is built from repeated plus -ly.
items.exampleCN: repeatedly 由 repeated 加 -ly 构成。
