definition_zh: 国王；君主；（纸牌中的）K；某领域最有影响者
definition_en: a man who rules a country by inherited right, and by extension the leading figure in some field
core_image: 王座上的人握着权杖，脚下铺着红毯
scene: 古堡大厅里，侍从把王冠捧到石阶之上。 The old king sat on the throne while the hall fell silent.
sceneCN: 这里 king 是「国王」（第 1 个义项：世袭统治一个国家的男子），句意是老国王坐在王座上，大厅随之安静下来。画面里有古堡大厅、王冠、石阶和红毯。

pos.zh: 某领域中最有影响力的人或物

derivatives.zh: king 加 -dom 构成，指王国、领域
king 加 -ly 构成，指君王般的、威严的
king 加 -ship 构成，指王位、王者身份
king 与 fisher 合成的鸟名，传说为水上的「渔王」
king 与 pin 合成，原指车轴主销，今喻组织中关键人物

senses.title: A man who rules by inherited right
senses.definition: a man who rules a country because he inherited the position
senses.definitionCN: 因继承而统治一个国家的男子
senses.example: The king ruled for forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 那位国王在位四十年。
senses.why: The word began as the name of a tribal chieftain, and kingship stayed a matter of birth rather than election.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初指部落首领，而王位始终靠出身而非推举。

senses.title: The leading ruler of a nation
senses.definition: the head of state in a monarchy, whether ruling or symbolic
senses.definitionCN: 君主制国家的元首，或掌实权或仅作象征
senses.example: The king opens parliament each year.
senses.exampleCN: 国王每年为议会揭幕。
senses.why: As monarchies became constitutional, the same title kept its place while its power shrank to ceremony.
senses.whyCN: 君主立宪之后，同一称号保留下来，而权力缩小到仪式层面。

senses.title: The highest playing card
senses.definition: the card ranking just below the ace in a suit
senses.definitionCN: 同一花色中仅次于 A 的高牌
senses.example: He laid down the king of hearts.
senses.exampleCN: 他甩出了红桃 K。
senses.why: Card games copied social ranks, so the top of the court cards bears the ruler's name.
senses.whyCN: 纸牌游戏照搬社会等级，所以花牌最上面那张用了君主的名字。

senses.title: The most important chess piece
senses.definition: the piece that must be protected, though it moves only one square
senses.definitionCN: 必须被保护的那个棋子，虽然每步只走一格
senses.example: Losing the king ends the game.
senses.exampleCN: 丢了王，棋局就结束。
senses.why: The chess piece is named for the ruler because the whole contest revolves around protecting him.
senses.whyCN: 这个棋子以君主命名，因为整盘棋都围绕保护他展开。

senses.title: The dominant figure in a field
senses.definition: the person or firm thought to be the best or most powerful in an area
senses.definitionCN: 被认为是某方面最出色或最有势力的人或企业
senses.example: He was once the king of late-night radio.
senses.exampleCN: 他曾是深夜广播的王者。
senses.why: Because a king stands at the top of a hierarchy, the word transfers to any field with a top spot.
senses.whyCN: 因为国王处在等级顶端，这个词就挪用到任何有高下之分的地方。

senses.title: The largest size of something
senses.definition: an unusually large version of a product, as in king-size
senses.definitionCN: 比通常更大的商品规格，如特大号床
senses.example: They sleep in a king-size bed.
senses.exampleCN: 他们睡一张特大号床。
senses.why: Advertisers borrowed royal rank to mean bigger than the others, an old habit in trade names.
senses.whyCN: 商家借王者的等级来表示「比别的大」，这是商品名里由来已久的习惯。

senses.title: The figure who presides at a festivity
senses.definition: someone chosen to play the ruler in a game or celebration, such as a carnival king
senses.definitionCN: 在游戏或庆典中被选来扮演统治者的人，如狂欢节的王
senses.example: The carnival king waved from the float.
senses.exampleCN: 狂欢节的王在花车上挥手。
senses.why: Festivals have long borrowed royal titles for temporary honour, so the word became a role anyone can hold for a night.
senses.whyCN: 节庆早已借用帝王头衔来给人一时的荣誉，于是这个词成了一个谁都能当晚扮演的角色。

senses.title: The male of a bee or ant colony
senses.definition: an old term for the reproductive male of some social insects
senses.definitionCN: 旧时对某些社会性昆虫繁殖雄性的称呼
senses.example: Older books speak of a bee king.
senses.exampleCN: 较早的书里提到「蜂王」时指雄蜂。
senses.why: Early observers assumed every colony had a ruler, so they named a king before they recognised the female queen.
senses.whyCN: 早期观察者以为每个群体都有一个统治者，在认出女王之前先用「王」来称呼。

intro.en: King is one of the oldest Germanic words in English, a family and tribal title that predates the word country itself.
intro.cn: king 是英语里最古老的日耳曼词之一，是比「国家」这个词还早的家族与部落称号。

items.en: The Germanic form kuningaz meant a man of the kin, the head of a clan.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形式 kuningaz 意为「同族之人中的头领」，即氏族之长。

items.en: In Old English the word was cyning, and it named the ruler of a people rather than of a state.
items.cn: 古英语里这个词作 cyning，指的是一个民族的统治者而不是国家的元首。

items.en: Religious writing extended the title to God, giving phrases such as king of heaven.
items.cn: 宗教文本把这一称号扩用于上帝，产生「天国之君」一类说法。

items.en: The form settled as king, and the plural became kings.
items.cn: 词形固定为 king，复数作 kings。

items.en: With constitutional monarchy the title kept its rank while political power moved to parliament.
items.cn: 君主立宪之后，这一称号保住位次，政治权力则转往议会。

items.en: The word spread into cards, chess, and commerce as a label for whatever stands at the top.
items.cn: 这个词又扩到纸牌、象棋和商业里，泛指处在顶端者。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words formed from the same root and the same court; the near-meaning group holds other titles of authority.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一词根和同一宫廷体系构成的词；近义组收其他表示权力的称号。

entries.definition: The realm a king rules, built with -dom.
entries.definitionCN: 国王所统治的疆域，加 -dom 构成。

entries.definition: Family, the older sense inside the word for king.
entries.definitionCN: 亲族，是 king 一词内层更早的含义。

entries.definition: Fit for a king, royal in manner.
entries.definitionCN: 君王般的、威严的。

entries.definition: The female ruler, from an unrelated old root.
entries.definitionCN: 指女性君主，词根不同，与 king 成对使用。

entries.definition: A single ruler of a state, the general term.
entries.definitionCN: 指国家唯一的统治者，是最概括的说法。

entries.definition: A ruler above kings, historically of an empire.
entries.definitionCN: 指高于国王的统治者，历史上多与帝国相连。

entries.definition: The leader of a clan or tribe, close to the earliest sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指氏族或部落首领，接近 king 最早的义项。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build from the clan head, through the court, to cards and commerce.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从氏族之长出发，经过宫廷，走到牌桌与商场。

normal.en: King and kin share a root: a king is the head of the kin.
normal.cn: king 与 kin 同根：王就是族人中的头。

normal.en: The -dom in kingdom means domain and state.
normal.cn: kingdom 里的 -dom 表示领域与国度。

normal.en: Kingship is the office, king the person.
normal.cn: kingship 指王位这个职位，king 指人。

normal.en: The king in cards sits just under the ace.
normal.cn: 牌里的 K 正好排在 A 之下。

normal.en: King-size means the biggest size sold.
normal.cn: king-size 就是能买到的最大号。

abstract.en: A crown is a circle worn on the head, a shape the whole people could wear.
abstract.cn: 王冠是戴在一人头上的圆圈，而那个圈本来人人可戴。

abstract.en: A king in chess moves one square and rules the whole board.
abstract.cn: 象棋里的王一步只走一格，却统辖整个棋盘。

abstract.en: Titles drift from thrones to shop windows without changing their shape.
abstract.cn: 称号从王座漂到橱窗，形状却一点没变。

examples.en: The king gave the land to his younger son.
examples.cn: 国王把这片土地给了小儿子。

examples.en: She drew the king of spades on the last turn.
examples.cn: 最后一轮她摸到了黑桃 K。

examples.en: This city is the king of northern ports.
examples.cn: 这座城市是北方港口之王。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坑」—— 王坐的深坑只有一个人能坐，别人下去就出不来

root: 日耳曼语 kuningaz，意为「同族中的头领」，古英语作 cyning，由 cynn（族）派生；后由氏族之长扩指国家君主，并借到纸牌、棋类与商业中表「顶端」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses: the inherited ruler, the constitutional head, the top card, the chess piece, the leader of a field, the largest size, the festival role, and the old name for a bee colony male.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项：世袭统治者、立宪元首、最高牌、棋子、领域之王、最大号、节庆角色，以及旧书里对蜂群雄性的称呼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one figure above the assembled kin, holding the staff.
core.cn: 核心意象：族人围聚之中，一人立于其上，手握权杖。

branches.en: THE THRONE LINE: from clan chief to constitutional head.
branches.cn: 王座这条线：从部落首领到立宪元首。

branches.en: THE GAME LINE: the title copied onto cards and boards.
branches.cn: 游戏这条线：称号被搬上牌桌和棋盘。

branches.en: THE MARKET LINE: whatever is biggest borrows the royal rank.
branches.cn: 市场这条线：最大的东西借用王者等级。

branches.en: THE FESTIVAL LINE: a ruler for one night.
branches.cn: 节庆这条线：当一晚的统治者。

branches.en: THE HIVE LINE: a mistaken king before the queen was found.
branches.cn: 蜂巢这条线：在认出女王之前误认的王。

intro.en: King is a native root that builds freely with -dom, -ly, -ship, and compounds, which the items below lay out.
intro.cn: king 是本土词根，可自由加 -dom、-ly、-ship 并参与合成，下面逐条列出。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic with no Latin ancestry, so the Latin entries below are only Latin words for the same ruler.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根属日耳曼语，没有拉丁血统，下面的拉丁条目只是同为「君主」的拉丁词。

items.example: The king called for his horse.
The kingdom stretched to the sea.
items.exampleCN: 这个王国一直延伸到海边。

items.example: A kingfisher flashed over the water.

items.meaning: a central pin or key person
items.example: He is the kingpin of the deal.
items.exampleCN: 他是这笔交易的关键人物。
它构成 kingdom 与 freedom。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉丁语「国王」，与 king 意义相当但不同源
拉丁语「王国、统治」，对应 kingdom 一义

definition_zh: 北；北方；北部；北面；北方的；向北
definition_en: the compass direction opposite to south and toward the North Pole; also the northern part of a country, and a position or movement facing that way
core_image: 指南针的针稳稳指向地图上方，那里的天空发白、风又冷又硬
scene: 清晨的站台上，风向标被风推得直指一侧，等车的人把围巾又绕了一圈。 A cold wind came down from the north, and everyone turned their backs to it.
sceneCN: 这里是「北方、北面」（第 1 个义项：罗盘上指向北极的方向），句意为一股冷风从北面吹来，人们都转过身背对着风。图中可辨识物件：风向标、围巾、站台长椅。

derivatives.zh: 由 north 加 -ern（属于某方向的）构成，义为「北方的；北部的」
由 north 加 -ward（朝……方向）构成，义为「向北」
由 north 加 -erly 构成，义为「偏北的；来自北方的」

senses.title: The compass direction toward the North Pole
senses.definition: the direction that is opposite to south and points toward the North Pole, one of the four main points of the compass
senses.definitionCN: 与南相反、指向北极的方向，是罗盘上四个主要方位之一
senses.example: A cold wind came down from the north, and everyone turned their backs to it.
senses.exampleCN: 一股冷风从北面吹来，人们都转过身背对着风。
senses.why: The Old English word named the direction to the left when a person faced the rising sun, and that left-hand side became the fixed compass point we still call north.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词命名的是面朝日出时左手边的那一侧，这一侧后来固定成罗盘上的方位，也就是今天的「北」。

senses.title: The northern part of a country or region
senses.definition: the part of a country, region or continent that lies furthest toward the north
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家、地区或大陆中最靠北的那一部分
senses.example: Her family moved to the north after the factory closed.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂关闭后，她家搬到了北部。
senses.why: Once north names a direction, the land lying in that direction can take the same name, so a country's cold upper half is simply called the north.
senses.whyCN: 既然 north 能指一个方向，位于那个方向上的土地也就用同一个词来称呼，于是一个国家寒冷的上一半就被叫作「北部」。

senses.title: The side or face that points north
senses.definition: the side of a building, hill or object that faces north, often the coolest or most shaded side
senses.definitionCN: 建筑物、山丘或物体朝北的一面，通常也是最凉、最背阴的一面
senses.example: The north face of the house stays in shadow most of the day.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋房子朝北的一面一天里大部分时间都在阴影里。
senses.why: A direction also marks one face of any object, so north shifted from a point on a map to a particular wall or slope, carrying its cold and shaded quality with it.
senses.whyCN: 方向也标出任何物体的某一个面，于是 north 从地图上的一个点转指某一面墙或某道山坡，同时把寒冷背阴的意味带了进去。

senses.title: Toward the north
senses.definition: in or toward the north, used mainly with verbs of movement
senses.definitionCN: 向北或在北方，主要与表示移动的动词连用
senses.example: They drove north along the coast for three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 他们沿着海岸向北开了三个小时。
senses.why: Because the word already fixes a destination, English can use it unchanged as an adverb of movement, and no separate form is needed for going that way.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词本身就固定了一个目的地，英语可以直接拿它当表示移动的副词，往那个方向走不必另造形式。

intro.en: North is a native Germanic word whose oldest recorded meaning is the direction on the left when one faces the rising sun; its deeper origin is reconstructed rather than certain.
intro.cn: north 是日耳曼语本土词，最早可考的意思是面朝日出时左手边的那一侧；它更古老的来源属于重构，并不确定。

items.en: A commonly proposed root for this group meant left or below, the side to a person's left when facing the dawn; the reconstruction is uncertain and not accepted by every scholar.
items.cn: 一般认为，这一族词有一个词根表示「左」或「下方」，即面朝晨光时人的左手边；这一重构并不确定，也并非所有学者都接受。

items.en: The Germanic form kept the sense of a left-hand direction and added a comparative ending, so the ancestor of north meant roughly the more leftward side.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形式保留了「左手边方向」的意思，并加了一个比较级词尾，因此 north 的祖先大致表示「更靠左的一侧」。

items.en: Norþ was the ordinary word for the direction and also stood in compounds for northern places and peoples.
items.cn: norþ 是表示这个方向的常用词，也出现在指北方地点与部族的复合词里。

items.en: Middle English settled the spelling as north and used it for the compass point, the northern region and the adjective.
items.cn: 中古英语把拼写固定为 north，并用它表示罗盘方位、北部地区以及形容词。

items.en: Modern English adds the adverb use, the phrase north of, and capitalized names such as the North Pole and the North Sea.
items.cn: 现代英语增添了副词用法、north of 这一说法，以及 North Pole、North Sea 这类首字母大写的名称。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family built on the same direction word; the near-meaning group puts north against the other compass points and the cold region it names.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一个方位词上的词族；近义组把 north 与其他方位词以及它所命名的寒冷地区放在一起对照。

entries.definition: Built on north with the -ern suffix, meaning of or in the north.
entries.definitionCN: 由 north 加 -ern 构成，义为「北方的；在北部的」。

entries.definition: North plus -ward, moving in the direction of the north.
entries.definitionCN: north 加 -ward，表示朝北移动。

entries.definition: A wind or direction coming from or pointing toward the north.
entries.definitionCN: 来自北方或指向北方的风或方向。

entries.definition: The compass point directly opposite north, toward the South Pole.
entries.definitionCN: 与 north 正相反、指向南极的罗盘方位。

entries.definition: Of the far north and the cold region around the North Pole.
entries.definitionCN: 指极北地区以及北极圈附近的寒冷地带。

entries.definition: Of the poles, the two ends of the earth's axis where the cold is deepest.
entries.definitionCN: 指地球自转轴两端、最寒冷的极地。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as the left-hand side of the sunrise and ends as a fixed compass point, and every later use keeps that same cold direction.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从日出时的左手边开始，最后固定成罗盘上的一个点，后来的每一种用法都保留着同一个寒冷的方向。

normal.en: Old English norþ named the left side of a person facing the rising sun, so the word's first job was to point at a side of the sky.
normal.cn: 古英语 norþ 指的是面朝日出时人的左手边，所以这个词最初的任务是指向天空的一侧。

normal.en: The Germanic ending on its ancestor was comparative, which is why north can be understood as the more leftward direction.
normal.cn: 它祖先身上的日耳曼语词尾是比较级，所以 north 可以理解为「更靠左的那个方向」。

normal.en: Northern is north plus -ern, a suffix that means belonging to a direction, as in western and southern.
normal.cn: northern 是 north 加 -ern，这个词尾表示「属于某个方向」，western 与 southern 也是这样构成的。

normal.en: Northward adds -ward, the suffix for movement toward a place, so the word itself says going that way.
normal.cn: northward 加了 -ward，这个词尾表示「朝某处移动」，所以词本身就在说「往那边走」。

normal.en: North of is a fixed way to locate a place, as in a village north of the river.
normal.cn: north of 是给地点定位的固定说法，例如「a village north of the river」这样的表达。

abstract.en: A compass point that started as a person's left hand shows how a word can move from the body to the map without changing its meaning.
abstract.cn: 一个从人的左手开始的方位词，展示了词如何从身体移到地图上，而意思并不改变。

abstract.en: Coldness clings to north because the direction itself brings the polar air, so the word carries weather inside its meaning.
abstract.cn: 寒冷一直黏在 north 上，因为那个方向本身就带来极地的空气，这个词把天气装进了自己的意思里。

abstract.en: Every use of north, from a wall to a whole region, is the same arrow pointing at one end of the world.
abstract.cn: north 的每一种用法，从一面墙到一整片地区，都是同一支指向世界一端的箭。

examples.en: A cold wind came down from the north, and everyone turned their backs to it.
examples.cn: 一股冷风从北面吹来，人们都转过身背对着风。

examples.en: The village lies north of the river, about a mile from the bridge.
examples.cn: 村子在河以北，离桥大约一英里。

examples.en: The north face of the house stays in shadow most of the day.
examples.cn: 这栋房子朝北的一面一天里大部分时间都在阴影里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺斯」——指南针上的针总往那个方向倒，风也从那边来；north 就是北方。

root: 古英语 norþ（面朝日出时的左手边），一般认为源自原始印欧语中表示「左、下方」的词根；词义固定为「北方」，并派生出 northern、northward、northerly 等。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the compass direction toward the pole; it then splits into the northern part of a place, the north-facing side of an object, and movement in that direction.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是指向极地的罗盘方位；义项由此分出某地的北部、物体朝北的一面，以及朝那个方向的移动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a compass needle locked on the top of the map, where the sky is pale and the wind is hard.
core.cn: 核心意象：指南针的针定在地图上方，那里天空发白、风又冷又硬。

branches.en: a compass needle swinging toward the top of the map
branches.cn: 指南针的针摆向地图上方

branches.en: a cold wind arriving from the polar dark
branches.cn: 极地暗处刮来的冷风

branches.en: a fishing town on the northern coast
branches.cn: 北方海岸上的渔村

branches.en: the shaded face of a hill turned away from the sun
branches.cn: 山丘背阴的那一面

branches.en: birds moving toward the top of the map
branches.cn: 候鸟朝地图上方飞去

intro.en: The word is held together by an Old English direction noun and the English endings that build its adjective, its motion adverb and its wind adjective.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语的方位名词，以及构成形容词、移动副词和风向形容词的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: North is a Germanic direction word with no reliable Latin cognate, so no Latin entry is listed.
latinIntro.cn: north 是日耳曼语的方位词，没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因此不列拉丁词条。

definition_zh: 第十九；第十九的；十九分之一；（某月的）十九日
definition_en: the ordinal number that comes after the eighteenth; one of nineteen equal parts; the nineteenth day of a month
core_image: 一排十九级台阶，最后一级上放着一支点亮的蜡烛
scene: 黄昏的走廊里排着十九级台阶，最后一级上放着一支点亮的蜡烛。 Her birthday falls on the nineteenth of May.
sceneCN: 这里是「某月的十九日」（第 3 个义项：一个月里编号为十九的那天）；句意为她的生日在五月十九日。图中可辨识物件：十九级台阶、蜡烛、走廊的扶手。

pos.zh: 十九分之一；（某月的）十九日

derivatives.zh: 由 nineteenth 加 -ly 构成，义为「第十九（用于列举）」
由 nineteenth 与 century 复合而成，义为「十九世纪的」

senses.title: The ordinal number after the eighteenth
senses.definition: the number that comes after the eighteenth in a counted series
senses.definitionCN: 在计数序列中排在第十八之后的数
senses.example: She finished nineteenth in a field of forty runners.
senses.exampleCN: 她在四十名跑者中排名第十九。
senses.why: Nineteenth is nine plus -teen plus -th: the teen ending marks ten added to a unit, and the ordinal ending marks a place in a line, so the word counts the spot just before twenty.
senses.whyCN: nineteenth 是 nine 加 -teen 再加 -th：-teen 表示十加个位数，序数词尾 -th 标出它在一列中的位置，所以这个词数的正是紧挨二十之前的那一位。

senses.title: One of nineteen equal parts
senses.definition: each of the nineteen equal parts into which a whole can be divided
senses.definitionCN: 把整体分成十九等份时其中的一份
senses.example: A nineteenth of the profit went to the local fund.
senses.exampleCN: 利润的十九分之一拨给了本地基金。
senses.why: The same ordinal ending that ranks an item also cuts a whole into that many pieces, so a nineteenth is the share created by dividing by nineteen.
senses.whyCN: 标出名次的序数词尾，同时也把整体切成同样多的份，所以 a nineteenth 就是被十九除开之后得到的那一份。

senses.title: The nineteenth day of a month
senses.definition: the day of a month numbered nineteenth, used mostly in dates
senses.definitionCN: 一个月中编号为十九的那一天，多用于日期
senses.example: The office reopens on the nineteenth.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室在十九日重新开放。
senses.why: Dates are a list of days, so the ordinal that ranks an item in a series doubles as the name of a particular day; English drops the noun day and lets the ordinal stand alone.
senses.whyCN: 日期本身就是一串日子，因此在序列里排位的序数词也兼作某一天的名称；英语省掉 day，直接让序数词单独站立。

intro.en: Nineteenth is a native English compound of nine, the teen ending and the ordinal ending, and it belongs to the Germanic number words that English never borrowed from Latin.
intro.cn: nineteenth 是英语本土的复合词，由 nine、表示十几的词尾和序数词尾构成，属英语从未向拉丁语借用的日耳曼数词。

items.en: The Germanic numeral for nine is reconstructed from its later descendants; its exact shape is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 日耳曼语的「九」是依据后来的后代形式重构出来的；它的确切形状只是重构，不是有记录的词。

items.en: Nigon was the Old English word for nine, and it stands at the base of nineteen, ninety and nineteenth alike.
items.cn: nigon 是古英语的「九」，也是 nineteen、ninety 与 nineteenth 共同的底座。

items.en: The ending -tīene or -tēne meant ten more, so nigontīene counted nine beyond ten.
items.cn: 词尾 -tīene 或 -tēne 表示「又多十」，因此 nigontīene 数的是十之后再添九。

items.en: The ordinal added the -tha ending used for ranking, producing the ancestor of nineteenth.
items.cn: 序数形式加上用于排位的词尾 -tha，形成 nineteenth 的祖先。

items.en: Modern English spells the compound nineteenth and uses it for rank, for a nineteenth part, and for the nineteenth day of a month.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个复合词写作 nineteenth，用来表示名次、十九分之一，以及某月的十九日。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the same nine base through its cardinal, tens and ordinal forms; the near-meaning group places nineteenth between its neighbours on the counting line.
note.cn: 形近组沿着同一个「九」的底座，收它的基数、十位与序数形式；近义组把 nineteenth 放回计数序列，看它前后相邻的词。

entries.definition: The cardinal before nineteenth, built on the same nine and teen elements.
entries.definitionCN: nineteenth 之前的基数词，由同样的 nine 与 teen 成分构成。

entries.definition: The ordinal for ninety, formed from ninety with the same -th ending used here.
entries.definitionCN: 九十的序数词，由 ninety 加同一个 -th 词尾构成。

entries.definition: The ordinal for nine, the smallest member of the same ordinal family.
entries.definitionCN: 九的序数词，是同一序数词族里最小的一员。

entries.definition: The tens form of nine, built with the -ty ending rather than -teen.
entries.definitionCN: 九的十位形式，用 -ty 词尾而不是 -teen。

entries.definition: The ordinal immediately before nineteenth in the same counting line.
entries.definitionCN: 同一计数序列中紧挨在第十九之前的序数词。

entries.definition: The ordinal immediately after nineteenth, closing the teens.
entries.definitionCN: 紧挨在第十九之后的序数词，为十几这一段的结尾。

entries.definition: The ending shared by the numbers thirteen to nineteen, the group nineteenth belongs to.
entries.definitionCN: 十三到十九共用的词尾，正是 nineteenth 所属的那一组。

entries.definition: A number word that marks position in a series, the class to which nineteenth belongs.
entries.definitionCN: 标出序列中位置的数词，是 nineteenth 所属的类别。

normalIntro.en: The word stacks three small pieces of English counting, a unit, a ten and a rank ending, and each piece explains one of its uses.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把英语计数的三个小零件叠在一起：一个个位数、一个「十」和一个表名次的词尾，每个零件都解释了它的一种用法。

normal.en: Nineteen is nine plus ten, so nineteenth is the ordinal of the number that sits one step before twenty.
normal.cn: 十九就是九加十，所以 nineteenth 是紧挨二十之前那个数的序数形式。

normal.en: The -teen ending means ten added to a unit, while -ty in ninety means tens; nineteenth follows the first pattern.
normal.cn: 词尾 -teen 表示十加个位数，而 ninety 里的 -ty 表示若干个十；nineteenth 走的是前一种模式。

normal.en: The -th ending turns a count into a rank, the same ending heard in fourth and twentieth.
normal.cn: 词尾 -th 把计数变成名次，和 fourth、twentieth 里听到的是同一个词尾。

normal.en: A nineteenth can also be a part, because dividing a whole by nineteen creates nineteen equal shares.
normal.cn: a nineteenth 也可以是一份，因为把整体按十九去分，就得到十九个相等的份。

normal.en: Dates use the bare ordinal, so on the nineteenth means on the nineteenth day of the month.
normal.cn: 日期直接用序数词，所以 on the nineteenth 就是在这个月的第十九天。

abstract.en: Nineteen is the last number before the round twenty, so its ordinal always sounds like a step just short of a clean boundary.
abstract.cn: 十九是整数二十之前的最后一个数，所以它的序数听起来总像差一步就到干净边界。

abstract.en: The same word can rank a runner, cut a cake into nineteen pieces and name a day, because English lets one ordinal do the work of position, fraction and date.
abstract.cn: 同一个词可以给跑者排名、把蛋糕切成十九份、还给某一天命名，因为英语让一个序数词同时承担位置、分数和日期三件事。

abstract.en: Counting words are the skeleton of a language, and nineteenth shows how a unit, a ten and a rank ending stack into one short word.
abstract.cn: 计数词是语言的骨架，而 nineteenth 展示了「一个个位数、一个十、一个名次词尾」如何叠成一个短词。

examples.en: She finished nineteenth in a field of forty runners.
examples.cn: 她在四十名跑者中排名第十九。

examples.en: A nineteenth of the profit went to the local fund.
examples.cn: 利润的十九分之一拨给了本地基金。

examples.en: The office reopens on the nineteenth.
examples.cn: 办公室在十九日重新开放。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奈恩婷丝」——数到十九级台阶，最后一级亮着蜡烛；nineteenth 就是第十九。

root: 古英语 nigon（九）加 -tīene（十）构成 nigontīene（十九），再加序数词尾 -tha 成为 nigontēontha；现代英语写作 nineteenth，属日耳曼语系本土数词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a rank just before twenty; the same form then serves as a nineteenth part and as the nineteenth day of a month.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是紧挨二十之前的一个名次；同一个形式再兼作十九分之一和某月的十九日。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of nineteen steps with a lit candle standing on the last one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排十九级台阶，最后一级上立着一支点亮的蜡烛。

branches.en: a runner crossing the line in nineteenth place
branches.cn: 跑者以第十九名冲过终点线

branches.en: the last step before a round twentieth
branches.cn: 紧挨整数二十之前的最后一级

branches.en: a cake cut into nineteen equal slices
branches.cn: 蛋糕被切成十九等份

branches.en: a share of the profit marked on a calendar page
branches.cn: 利润的一份被记在日历的某一页上

branches.en: a notice on the door announcing the nineteenth
branches.cn: 门上贴出十九日重开的通知

intro.en: The word is assembled from the Old English nine, the teen suffix that adds ten, the ordinal ending and the English endings it still takes.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语的「九」、表示「再加十」的词尾、序数词尾，以及它至今仍在使用的英语词尾组装而成。

latinIntro.en: English nine descends from the same ancient Indo-European numeral as Latin novem, so the Latin forms are cognates for comparison, not the source of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 英语的 nine 与拉丁语 novem 同出古老的原始印欧语数词，因此下列拉丁形式只供对照，并不是英语这个词的来源。

definition_zh: 清洁工；清洁剂；清洁器；更干净的
definition_en: a person whose job is cleaning; a substance or machine used for cleaning; the comparative of clean
core_image: 推着拖把的车，把楼道擦亮的人
scene: 清晨的走廊里，保洁阿姨推着水车慢慢走过。 The cleaner washed the floor before class.
sceneCN: 这里 cleaner 是「清洁工」（第 1 个义项：以打扫为业的人）；句意是上课前清洁工清洗了地板。

pos.zh: 更干净的（clean 的比较级）

derivatives.zh: cleaner 的基础词，义为「干净的」
由 clean 加后缀 -ing 构成，义为「清扫；清洁工作」
由 clean 加后缀 -ness 构成，义为「清洁」

senses.title: A person whose job is cleaning
senses.definition: a person employed to keep places clean
senses.definitionCN: 受雇保持场所干净的人
senses.example: The cleaner arrives at six every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 清洁工每天早晨六点到位。
senses.why: The agent suffix -er turns the action into the doer.
senses.whyCN: 施动后缀 -er 把动作变成做动作的人。

senses.title: A substance or machine for cleaning
senses.definition: a product or device used to remove dirt
senses.definitionCN: 用来清除污垢的物品或装置
senses.example: Spray some cleaner on the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 往桌上喷点清洁剂。
senses.why: The same suffix names a tool that performs the action.
senses.whyCN: 同一个后缀也命名执行该动作的工具。

senses.title: The comparative of clean
senses.definition: more clean than something else
senses.definitionCN: 比另一物更干净
senses.example: This classroom is cleaner than ours.
senses.exampleCN: 这间教室比我们的干净。
senses.why: Adding -er to the adjective builds its comparative form.
senses.whyCN: 形容词加 -er 构成比较级形式。

intro.en: Cleaner simply adds the old agent suffix -er to clean.
intro.cn: cleaner 就是在 clean 后加上古老的施动后缀 -er。

items.en: Old English clæne meant clean and pure.
items.cn: 古英语 clæne 义为干净、纯洁。

items.en: Old English -ere was a suffix for the person doing something.
items.cn: 古英语后缀 -ere 表示做某事的人。

items.en: Middle English combined them as clenere, a person who cleans.
items.cn: 中古英语合为 clenere，指打扫的人。

items.en: Modern English kept cleaner for people and tools alike.
items.cn: 现代英语用 cleaner 兼指人和工具。

items.en: The comparative use of cleaner grew alongside.
items.cn: cleaner 的比较级用法随之发展。

note.en: The first group gathers cleaning words; the second gathers look-alikes.
note.cn: 第一组收清洁类词，第二组收形近词。

entries.definition: The most clean.
entries.definitionCN: clean 的最高级形式。

entries.definition: The comparative of clear.
entries.definitionCN: clear 的比较级，词形与 cleaner 相近。

entries.definition: The comparative of lean.
entries.definitionCN: lean 的比较级，拼写与 cleaner 接近。

entries.definition: A shop that cleans clothes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「干洗店」，常用复数形式。

entries.definition: A person cleaning a building, American usage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，美式义为「大楼清洁管理员」。

entries.definition: A soap powder for washing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「洗涤剂」，与清洁剂同类。

normalIntro.en: Remember cleaner through its two jobs.
normalIntro.cn: 记住 cleaner 的两种身份。

normal.en: cleaner can be a person or a product.
normal.cn: cleaner 可指人也可指清洁剂。

normal.en: -er marks the doer of an action.
normal.cn: -er 标记动作的执行者。

normal.en: vacuum cleaner is the machine for floors.
normal.cn: vacuum cleaner 指吸尘器。

normal.en: cleaner is also the comparative of clean.
normal.cn: cleaner 也是 clean 的比较级。

normal.en: the cleaner's means the dry-cleaning shop.
normal.cn: the cleaner's 指干洗店。

abstract.en: See a mop swinging across a long corridor.
abstract.cn: 想象拖把在长走廊上来回摆动。

abstract.en: Hear the soft hum of a vacuum at dawn.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见清晨吸尘器的低鸣。

abstract.en: Feel fresh air after a wiped window opens.
abstract.cn: 感受擦净的窗户打开后的清新空气。

examples.en: Our school cleaner keeps the hall bright.
examples.cn: 学校的清洁工把大厅保持得很明亮。

examples.en: Add a little cleaner to the water.
examples.cn: 往水里加一点清洁剂。

examples.en: After the rain, the streets are much cleaner.
examples.cn: 雨后街道干净多了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「克立纳」——克立的纳凉亭由清洁工擦得干干净净。

root: clean（古英语 clæne，干净）+ -er（古英语 -ere，施动者后缀）→ 中古英语 clenere → 现代英语 cleaner；兼作 clean 的比较级。

sensesIntro.en: Cleaner names the person who cleans, the product that cleans and the comparative form.
sensesIntro.cn: cleaner 兼指打扫的人、清洁用品和 clean 的比较级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the one or thing that brings cleanness
core.cn: 核心意象：带来洁净的那个人或物

branches.cn: 比之前更干净

branches.cn: 楼宇里的一个岗位

branches.en: A bottle on the shelf
branches.cn: 货架上的清洁剂瓶

intro.en: The suffix -er does double duty in cleaner.
intro.cn: 后缀 -er 在 cleaner 中一符两用。

latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词根，-er 出自古英语。

items.meaning: a machine that sucks up dust

definition_zh: 使印象深刻；使钦佩；盖印；铭刻
definition_en: to make someone feel admiration, or to press or stamp something onto a surface
core_image: 一枚印章压进蜡面留下痕迹
scene: 面试官看着桌上的模型。 The candidate's handmade model impressed everyone in the room.
sceneCN: 这里 impress 是「使印象深刻、使钦佩」（第 1 个义项：产生赞赏的效果）；句意：应聘者手工制作的模型让在场每个人都印象深刻。

derivatives.zh: 印象；印痕；加名词后缀
令人赞叹的；加形容词后缀
被打动的；分词转形容词

senses.title: To fill with admiration
senses.definition: to make someone feel admiration or respect
senses.definitionCN: 使某人产生钦佩或敬意
senses.example: Her calm reply impressed the judges.
senses.exampleCN: 她沉着的回答令评委印象深刻。
senses.why: The stamp presses admiration into the mind as ink presses a seal.
senses.whyCN: 印章把钦佩压进脑海，如同印模压出图纹。

senses.title: To press or stamp
senses.definition: to press a mark or design onto a surface
senses.definitionCN: 在表面压出印记或图案
senses.example: The clerk impressed the seal on the certificate.
senses.exampleCN: 职员在证书上盖了印章。
senses.why: The literal act: hard contact leaves a copy of itself.
senses.whyCN: 字面动作：坚硬的接触留下自身的复制品。

senses.title: To fix firmly in the mind
senses.definition: to make an idea stay firmly in someone's mind
senses.definitionCN: 使某个想法牢牢留在心中
senses.example: The coach impressed discipline on the team.
senses.exampleCN: 教练让纪律深植全队心中。
senses.why: The seal is applied to memory: the mark will not wipe away.
senses.whyCN: 印章盖在记忆上：痕迹擦不掉。

senses.title: To use as a show
senses.definition: to perform in order to win admiration, often insincerely
senses.definitionCN: 为赢得赞赏而表现，常不真诚
senses.example: He bought the car just to impress the neighbors.
senses.exampleCN: 他买车只是为了给邻居留下深刻印象。
senses.why: The stamp is forged: admiration aimed at appearance, not truth.
senses.whyCN: 印章是伪造的：针对表象而非真相的钦佩。

senses.title: To compel by force (historic impressment)
senses.definition: to force someone into service, as sailors were impressed
senses.definitionCN: 强迫某人服役，如旧时强征水手
senses.example: The navy impressed young men into service.
senses.exampleCN: 海军强征年轻人入伍。
senses.why: The same pressing, applied to bodies instead of wax.
senses.whyCN: 同样的按压，从蜡面换成对人的强压。

intro.en: Impress comes from Latin imprimere, to press in or upon, from in- and premere, to press. The seal image explains every sense: pressing leaves a mark, and marks persuade.
intro.cn: impress 来自拉丁语 imprimere「压入」，由 in- 加 premere「压」构成。印章意象解释一切义项：按压留下痕迹，而痕迹能说服人。

items.en: Latin premere meant to press; imprimere meant to press into or upon something.
items.cn: 拉丁语 premere 意为压；imprimere 意为压入或压上。

items.en: The noun impressio named the mark left by pressing, in wax or in the mind.
items.cn: 名词 impressio 指按压留下的痕迹，或在蜡上，或在心里。

items.en: Old French empirer and later English borrowings kept the literal stamping.
items.cn: 古法语与后来的英语借词保留了字面的盖章义。

items.en: Middle English impress meant to stamp, then to fix in the mind.
items.cn: 中古英语 impress 先指盖章，继而指铭刻于心。

items.en: The admiration sense grew strong in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries; impressment named the forced naval recruitment.
items.cn: 钦佩义在十八九世纪壮大；impressment 则指强征水手。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the impress family and the historic impressment. The meaning group compares admiration and stamping words.
note.cn: 形近组区分 impress 词族与历史词 impressment；词义组比较钦佩与盖印类词。

entries.definition: the mark or feeling left behind.
entries.definitionCN: 印象；印痕。按压留下的东西。

entries.definition: the forced recruitment of sailors.
entries.definitionCN: 强征（旧义）。历史用法。

entries.definition: to state or send quickly. Nearly the same shape, opposite prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 表达；快递。形状几乎相同，前缀相反。

entries.definition: to impress so strongly that one is speechless.
entries.definitionCN: 使震惊。强到说不出话。

entries.definition: to affect strongly, as a thought striking someone.
entries.definitionCN: 打动。如想法击中某人。

entries.definition: to press a mark on paper or metal.
entries.definitionCN: 盖章。在纸或金属上压印。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the word into im + press, keep the wax-seal image and reuse impressed by.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩把词拆成 im 加 press，保留蜡封意象，并复用 impressed by。

normal.en: im + press: the world presses on you and leaves a mark.
normal.cn: im 加 press：世界压在你身上，留下印记。

normal.en: be impressed by is the standard passive frame.
normal.cn: be impressed by 是标准被动句型。

normal.en: impress on someone means to stamp an idea into memory.
normal.cn: impress on someone 指把想法盖进记忆。

normal.en: impressing the neighbors is the fake version of impressing.
normal.cn: impressing the neighbors 是 impress 的虚假版本。

normal.en: impressment pressed bodies, not wax; a dark historic sense.
normal.cn: impressment 压的是人不是蜡；黑暗的历史义项。

abstract.en: One image: a seal pressed into warm wax.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：印章压进温热的蜡。

abstract.en: To impress is to leave a mark that argues for you.
abstract.cn: impress 是留下一个替你说话的印记。

abstract.en: Marks differ: wax marks, mind marks, forged marks.
abstract.cn: 印记有别：蜡上的、心里的、伪造的。

examples.en: The documentary impressed me deeply.
examples.cn: 这部纪录片令我印象深刻。

examples.en: The jeweler impressed his mark into the gold.
examples.cn: 珠宝匠把标记压进金子里。

examples.en: She tried to impress the panel with her research.
examples.cn: 她试图用研究打动评审团。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「一姆普瑞斯」：一按，噗——印记落在你心里， impressed！

root: 拉丁语 in-（入）+ premere「压」→ imprimere「压入」→ impressio「印记」→ 古法语 → 中古英语 impress「盖章→铭刻于心」；现代英语以钦佩义为主。

sensesIntro.en: Impress presses: a seal into wax, an idea into memory, admiration into a mind, and, in history, men into ships.
sensesIntro.cn: impress 就是按压：印章入蜡、观念入心、钦佩入脑，历史上还有强征入伍。

core.en: Hard contact that leaves a lasting copy of itself.
core.cn: 坚硬的接触，留下自身持久的复制品。

branches.en: ADMIRATION: her reply impressed the judges.
branches.cn: 钦佩：她的回答令评委折服。

branches.en: STAMP: the seal impressed on the certificate.
branches.cn: 盖印：印章压上证书。

branches.en: MEMORY: impressing discipline on the team.
branches.cn: 记忆：让纪律深植全队。

branches.en: SHOW: impressing the neighbors on purpose.
branches.cn: 做秀：刻意给邻居留下印象。

branches.en: FORCE: impressment of sailors into the navy.
branches.cn: 强征：将水手强征入海军。

intro.en: Impress keeps the Latin press at its heart; the family adds impression, impressive, impressed and the partner express.
intro.cn: impress 的核心是拉丁语的「压」；词族加上 impression、impressive、impressed 及反前缀的 express。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the pressing verb and the noun for the mark it leaves.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示按压动词与其留下的印记名词。
